questions.stem: Warm is to torrid as cool is to
questions.explain: Torrid is the extreme form of warm, so the answer must be the extreme form of cool, which is frigid. Chilly is only a little colder than cool, so it is the right direction but the wrong degree. Tepid means lukewarm and moves back toward warm. Brisk and temperate describe mild, comfortable conditions, not an extreme.

questions.stem: Dislike is to loathe as admire is to
questions.explain: To loathe is to dislike intensely, so the answer must mean to admire intensely, which is revere. Respect is roughly the same strength as admire, so it misses the step up in degree. Envy is a different feeling, praise is an action rather than a feeling, and tolerate is weaker than admire.

questions.stem: Murmur is to roar as
questions.explain: A murmur is a faint sound and a roar is an intense sound of the same kind; likewise a glimmer is a faint light and a blaze is an intense light. Shout is to whisper runs the scale in the reverse direction. An echo comes from a sound (product to source), a glare causes a squint (cause and effect), and a spark is used to ignite (tool and action).

questions.stem: Glad is to jubilant as sad is to
questions.explain: Jubilant is an extreme degree of glad, so the answer must be an extreme degree of sad: despondent, meaning deeply dejected and without hope. Wistful is only a mild, longing sadness, so the degree is wrong. Cheerful is the opposite feeling, pensive means thoughtful, and irritable is a different emotion altogether.

questions.stem: Frugal is to miserly as
questions.explain: Frugal is a sensible quality and miserly is the same quality pushed to an unpleasant excess; confident pushed to excess becomes arrogant. Generous is to stingy, cautious is to reckless and bold is to timid are all opposites, not the same trait taken too far. Thrifty and economical are synonyms of equal strength, so there is no step up in degree.

questions.stem: Stanza is to poem as act is to
questions.explain: A stanza is a major division of a poem, and an act is a major division of a play. Scene reverses the levels, because a scene is a part of an act, not the whole that contains it. An actor performs in a play, a stage is where it is performed, and a sonnet is a kind of poem.

questions.stem: Vertebra is to spine as link is to
questions.explain: A vertebra is one of the repeated units that make up a spine, and a link is one of the repeated units that make up a chain. Connection is a synonym of link, not the whole it belongs to. An anchor is attached to a chain, a strand is a unit of rope, and a weld is a way of joining metal.

questions.stem: Phoneme is to word as note is to
questions.explain: Phonemes are the basic units of sound that combine to form a word, and notes are the basic units that combine to form a melody. Pitch is a property of a single note, not the larger whole it builds. Tempo is the speed of music, the staff is where notes are written, and a composer is the person who writes them.

questions.stem: Pixel is to image as
questions.explain: A pixel is the basic building block of a digital image, just as a cell is the basic building block of an organism. A brush is a tool applied to a canvas and a frame surrounds a portrait, so neither is a building block. A negative is the source a print is made from, and focus and blur are opposites.

questions.stem: Petal is to flower as
questions.explain: A petal is one of the parts that make up a flower, and a feather is one of the parts that make up a wing. An acorn is food for a squirrel, nectar is the raw material bees turn into honey, and a root grows in soil. A gardener uses a rake, which is worker and tool.

questions.stem: Surgeon is to scalpel as sculptor is to
questions.explain: A surgeon uses a scalpel as the main cutting tool, and a sculptor uses a chisel. Statue is what the sculptor produces, not the tool. Marble and clay are materials the sculptor works on, and a studio is the place where the work is done.

questions.stem: Mason is to trowel as farrier is to
questions.explain: A mason uses a trowel to spread mortar, and a farrier, who shoes horses, uses a rasp to file the hoof level. The horseshoe is what the farrier fits (the product), and the hoof is what is worked on. A stable is where horses are kept, and a saddle is made by a saddler, not used by a farrier.

questions.stem: Astronomer is to telescope as
questions.explain: An astronomer uses a telescope as the instrument for observing, and a seismologist uses a seismograph as the instrument for recording earthquakes. A botanist studies plants and a geologist studies rocks, so those pairs give the subject studied, not the instrument. A forecast is what a meteorologist produces, and a cockpit is where a pilot works.

questions.stem: Barber is to clippers as
questions.explain: A barber cuts with clippers, and a tailor cuts with shears, so both pairs are worker and tool. A restaurant is where a chef works, not the tool. A novel and a harvest are what the worker produces, and a leak is the problem a plumber fixes.

questions.stem: Awl is to pierce as plane is to
questions.explain: An awl is a woodworking tool used to pierce holes, and a plane is a woodworking tool used to smooth wood. Fly is the trap: it fits an airplane, a different meaning of the word plane. A plane does not measure or join wood, and to bore a hole you would use a drill or auger.

questions.stem: Auger is to bore as strop is to
questions.explain: An auger is a tool used to bore holes, and a strop, a strip of leather, is a tool used to hone the edge of a razor. Razor is the object that gets honed, and leather is what the strop is made of. Shaving is what the razor does afterward, and the barber is the worker who uses the strop.

questions.stem: Lever is to pry as
questions.explain: A lever is a simple machine used to pry, and a wedge is a simple machine used to split. Hammer is to nail names the object the tool acts on, not the action, so it is the closest trap. A pulley works with a rope, a thread is part of a screw, and an axle is part of a wheel assembly.

questions.stem: Quill is to write as
questions.explain: A quill is used to write, and a loom is used to weave, so each pair is a tool and the action it performs. Needle is to thread pairs a tool with its material, saw is to lumber and oven is to bread pair a tool with what it produces, and a spool simply holds yarn.

questions.stem: Ceilometer is to cloud height as hygrometer is to
questions.explain: A ceilometer is the instrument that measures the height of the cloud base, and a hygrometer is the instrument that measures humidity, the amount of water vapor in the air. Rainfall is the hygro- (water) trap but is measured with a rain gauge, air pressure is read on a barometer, and temperature on a thermometer. Visibility is the ceiling-and-visibility trap carried over from the first pair and needs a visibility sensor, not a hygrometer.

questions.stem: Drought is to famine as flood is to
questions.explain: A drought can cause famine, and a flood can cause erosion, so the second word is a result of the first. Rain causes a flood, which reverses the direction. A dam is built to prevent floods, a river is where floods happen, and thirst is linked to drought, not flood.

questions.stem: Lightning is to thunder as earthquake is to
questions.explain: Lightning causes thunder, and an undersea earthquake can cause a tsunami. A fault is where an earthquake starts, so it is closer to a cause than an effect. A volcano is a separate geological event, magnitude is a measure of an earthquake's size, and a seismograph is the instrument that records it.

questions.stem: Negligence is to accident as
questions.explain: Negligence is a failing that leads to an accident, and fatigue is a condition that leads to an error. Injury is to carelessness puts the effect first, so the direction is reversed. Blunder and mistake are synonyms, a verdict is produced by a court, and a precaution guards against a hazard rather than causing it.

questions.stem: Virus is to infection as
questions.explain: A virus causes an infection, and a spark causes a fire. A doctor treats a patient and medicine treats an illness, so those pairs show treatment, not cause. A fever is measured with a thermometer and a wound is covered with a bandage.

questions.stem: Oxidation is to rust as fermentation is to
questions.explain: Oxidation of iron produces rust, and fermentation of sugar produces alcohol, so the second word is the product of the process. Yeast is the agent that carries out fermentation, and sugar is the starting material, so both sit on the wrong side of the process. A grape is a source of sugar, and a cellar is where wine is stored.

questions.stem: Mammal is to whale as reptile is to
questions.explain: A whale is a member of the category mammal, and a tortoise is a member of the category reptile. A frog is an amphibian, not a reptile, which makes it the closest trap. Amphibian is a neighboring category, not a member, and scales and eggs are features of reptiles rather than kinds of reptile.

questions.stem: Sonnet is to poem as sarcophagus is to
questions.explain: A sonnet is a specific kind of poem, and a sarcophagus is a specific kind of coffin, one carved from stone. A tomb is the place where a sarcophagus is kept, so it gives location, not category. A mummy is what lies inside it, a pharaoh is a person who might be buried in one, and a pyramid is a kind of tomb.

questions.stem: Cobalt is to element as
questions.explain: Cobalt is a member of the category element, and brass is a member of the category alloy. Alloy is to bronze has the right relationship but in the reverse order, with the category first. Ore is the source of a metal, an atom is part of a molecule, and copper is the material a wire is made from.

questions.stem: Utensil is to spatula as garment is to
questions.explain: A spatula is one kind of utensil, and a tunic is one kind of garment. Fabric is what a garment is made from, a wardrobe is where garments are stored, a tailor makes them, and a seam is part of one. Only tunic is a member of the category.

questions.stem: Sonata is to composition as
questions.explain: A sonata is one kind of musical composition, and a gavotte is one kind of dance, so each pair is member then category. Composition is to fugue has the right relationship but puts the category first. A movement is a part of a symphony, a composer produces a score, and a stage is where ballet is performed.

questions.stem: Thermostat is to temperature as metronome is to
questions.explain: A thermostat exists to regulate temperature, and a metronome exists to regulate tempo, the speed of music. Pitch is the musical quality a tuning fork sets, so it is the related-but-wrong trap. Music is the general activity, a pianist is a user of the device, and volume is controlled by other means.

questions.stem: Levee is to flood as
questions.explain: A levee is built to prevent a flood, and a vaccine is given to prevent a disease. A spark causes a fire and a storm causes damage, which is the opposite of preventing them. A thermometer measures a fever and a map shows a route.

questions.stem: Ballast is to stability as
questions.explain: Ballast is material added to a vessel to provide stability, and fertilizer is material added to soil to promote growth. An anchor prevents drift, so its pair names what it stops, not what it provides. A keel is part of a hull, a sail hangs on a mast, and a compass points north.

questions.stem: Catalyst is to reaction as
questions.explain: A catalyst is used to speed up a chemical reaction, and an accelerant is used to speed up combustion. An extinguisher puts out a flame, the opposite function. Fuel powers an engine rather than speeding up a process, a product is the result of a reaction, and a thermometer measures heat.

questions.stem: Larva is to pupa as tadpole is to
questions.explain: In an insect's life cycle the larva develops into the pupa, and in an amphibian's life cycle the tadpole develops into the frog. Egg is the stage before the tadpole, so it runs the sequence backward. A caterpillar is itself a larva, a pond is the tadpole's habitat, and a gill is a body part.

questions.stem: Prologue is to epilogue as overture is to
questions.explain: A prologue opens a literary work and an epilogue closes it; an overture opens a musical work and a finale closes it. Prelude is a synonym of overture, another opening piece, not the closing one. An intermission comes in the middle, an opera is the whole work, and an aria is a single song within it.

questions.stem: Bud is to blossom as
questions.explain: A bud is an earlier stage that develops into a blossom, and an embryo is an earlier stage that develops into a fetus. Fruit is to flower is in the same botanical topic but backward, because the flower comes before the fruit. A seed is planted in soil, pollen is carried by a bee, and an egg sits in a nest.

questions.stem: Freshman is to sophomore as
questions.explain: A freshman moves up to sophomore, the very next level, and an Air Force captain is promoted to major, the very next rank. Major is to captain runs the order backward, and captain is to colonel skips the ranks in between. A sergeant leads a squad, and a cadet attends an academy.

questions.stem: Sketch is to painting as rehearsal is to
questions.explain: A sketch is a preliminary version that comes before the finished painting, and a rehearsal is a preliminary run that comes before the finished performance. Practice is a synonym of rehearsal rather than what it leads to. An audition is a tryout for a role, a script is the text used, and a stage is the location.

questions.stem: Laconic is to verbose as candid is to
questions.explain: Laconic (using very few words) is the opposite of verbose (using too many words), so the answer must be the opposite of candid, which means open and direct; evasive fits. Frank, blunt and honest are all near-synonyms of candid. Talkative is a synonym of verbose, drawn from the first pair.

questions.stem: Exacerbate is to alleviate as
questions.explain: To exacerbate is to make worse and to alleviate is to make better, so the pair are opposites; augment (increase) and diminish (decrease) are also opposites. Aggravate and worsen are synonyms, as are soothe and relieve. Ease is to pain is an action and its object, and intensify and provoke both push in the same direction.

questions.stem: Scarce is to plentiful as transient is to
questions.explain: Scarce is the opposite of plentiful, and transient (passing quickly) is the opposite of permanent. Temporary and brief are synonyms of transient, not opposites. Migrant plays on transient's use as a noun for a person passing through, and abundant is a synonym of plentiful from the first pair.

questions.stem: Ephemeral is to perennial as
questions.explain: Ephemeral (lasting a very short time) is the opposite of perennial (lasting year after year), and novice (inexperienced) is the opposite of veteran (long experienced). Fleeting and brief are synonyms. A seedling grows into a tree (a stage), annual describes a yearly event on a calendar, and dusk is the start of evening, not its opposite.

questions.stem: Zenith is to nadir as
questions.explain: The zenith is the highest point and the nadir is the lowest point, so they are opposites; the apex is the top of a shape and the base is the bottom. Summit and peak are synonyms, as are noon and midday. A planet travels in an orbit, and the horizon is where the sky meets the land.

questions.stem: Hangar is to aircraft as apiary is to
questions.explain: A hangar is the place where aircraft are kept, and an apiary is the place where bees are kept. Honey is the product the bees make, not what the apiary houses. Birds are kept in an aviary, the look-alike word, the beekeeper is the worker, and flowers are where bees feed.

questions.stem: Eagle is to aerie as beaver is to
questions.explain: An aerie is the specific home an eagle builds and lives in, and a lodge is the specific home a beaver builds and lives in. A beaver also builds a dam, but the dam holds back water and is not its dwelling, which makes it the trap. A pond is the wider habitat, a kit is a young beaver, and timber is building material.

questions.stem: Cactus is to desert as
questions.explain: A cactus is a plant adapted to live in the desert, and a mangrove is a plant adapted to live in a swamp. Tundra is to moss has the right relationship in reverse, with the habitat first. A hump is part of a camel, a dune is made of sand, and a coconut is the fruit of a palm.

questions.stem: Pilot is to cockpit as
questions.explain: A cockpit is the place where a pilot works, and a kitchen is the place where a chef works. A captain leads a crew, a driver uses a steering wheel as a control (worker and tool), a nurse cares for a patient, and an author produces a manuscript. None of those pairs names a workplace.

questions.stem: Archive is to documents as arsenal is to
questions.explain: An archive is a place where documents are stored, and an arsenal is a place where weapons are stored. Soldiers use the weapons and war is the activity they serve, but neither is what an arsenal holds. A museum is another kind of storage building, and a fortress is a defended place, not its contents.

questions.stem: Wool is to sheep as silk is to
questions.explain: Wool is produced by sheep, and silk is produced by the silkworm. Cotton is another fiber, not a source. Satin is a fabric that can be woven from silk (a product of it, so the direction is wrong), mulberry leaves are what silkworms eat, and a loom is the tool that weaves the thread.

questions.stem: Pearl is to oyster as ambergris is to
questions.explain: A pearl is formed inside an oyster, and ambergris is a waxy substance formed in the gut of the sperm whale. Amber only sounds similar; it is fossilized tree resin, which is why resin is also a trap. Perfume is a product made from ambergris, which reverses the direction, and the shore is merely where it often washes up.

questions.stem: Paper is to pulp as glass is to
questions.explain: Paper is made from pulp, and glass is made from sand, so the second word is the raw material. Clay is the raw material for ceramics, not glass. A window and a mirror are products made from glass, which reverses the direction, and a furnace is the equipment used to melt it.

questions.stem: Vellum is to calf as
questions.explain: Vellum is a fine writing material made from the skin of a calf, and cashmere is a fine wool that comes from a goat, so each pair is product then animal source. Leather is to saddle reverses the direction, giving material then the thing made from it. Wool is worked on a loom, a calf is the young of a cow, and a hide is processed at a tannery.

questions.stem: Destitute is to money as anonymous is to
questions.explain: Someone destitute is without money, and something anonymous is without a name. Fame is the trap: an anonymous person may be unknown, but the word means lacking a name, not lacking celebrity. Author is a person who can be anonymous, while a secret and a mask are ways of hiding identity rather than what is absent.

questions.stem: Insipid is to flavor as inert is to
questions.explain: Something insipid lacks flavor, and something inert lacks motion (or the power to move or act). Mass is the trap from physics, because inertia depends on mass, but inert does not mean lacking mass. Gas and element come from inert gases, which are things that can be inert, not what inert means they lack, and color is unrelated.

questions.stem: Barren is to fertility as
questions.explain: Barren means lacking fertility, and mute means lacking speech. Arid and fallow describe a desert and a field, so they pair a quality with the thing it describes. Deaf means lacking hearing, not music, and fruitful means producing a harvest, the opposite of lacking.

questions.stem: Insomnia is to sleep as
questions.explain: Insomnia is the inability to sleep, and amnesia is the loss of memory, so each names a lack of the second word. A fever is an excess of temperature, the opposite of a lack. Dreams happen during sleep, nostalgia is a fond feeling about memories, and hunger is a lesser degree of famine.

questions.stem: Dove is to peace as owl is to
questions.explain: A dove is a symbol of peace, and an owl is a symbol of wisdom. Night is when owls are active and prey is what they hunt, so those are facts about the bird, not its meaning. A hawk is another bird, and war is what the hawk, not the owl, symbolizes.

questions.stem: Scepter is to sovereignty as gavel is to
questions.explain: A scepter is a symbol of a monarch's sovereignty, and a gavel is a symbol of a presiding officer's authority. Judge is the person who holds the gavel, not what it stands for, which makes it the main trap. A verdict is the outcome of a trial, a courtroom is the location, and hammer describes what a gavel physically is.

questions.stem: Laurel is to victory as
questions.explain: A laurel wreath is a symbol of victory, and a halo is a symbol of holiness. Crown is to head and trophy is to shelf give where the object is worn or kept, not what it stands for. A flag hangs on a pole, and an antidote counters a poison.

questions.stem: Olive branch is to peace as
questions.explain: An olive branch is a sign that signals peace, and a white flag is a sign that signals surrender. A dove is a member of the category bird, and a branch is part of a tree. A treaty ends a war, and a soldier uses a rifle as a tool.

questions.stem: Tepid is to scalding as damp is to
questions.explain: Scalding is the extreme form of tepid warmth, so the answer must be the extreme form of damp, which is sodden (soaked through). Moist is about the same degree as damp, so it misses the step up. Humid describes damp air, and dank means unpleasantly damp and cold, so both stay at the same level. Arid is the opposite of damp, not a stronger form of it.

questions.stem: Pique is to fury as
questions.explain: Pique is mild irritation and fury is the extreme of the same feeling. Apprehension is mild fear and terror is its extreme, so the pair rises in degree in the same order. Exasperation is to annoyance runs from strong to mild, the reverse. Grief causes tears, panic is the opposite of composure, and envy is a feeling directed at a rival, so none is a step up in intensity.

questions.stem: Nudge is to shove as sip is to
questions.explain: A shove is a much more forceful nudge, so the answer must be a much bigger sip, which is gulp. Nibble is a small bite of food, the same small degree in a different action. Taste and savor are gentle ways of trying a drink, and drink is the general action that covers both sip and gulp, so none of them is the stronger form.

questions.stem: Fuselage is to aircraft as hull is to
questions.explain: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft, and the hull is the main body of a ship. Keel and sail are also parts of a ship, so they give a part where the whole is needed. An anchor is equipment a ship carries, and a harbor is where it is kept.

questions.stem: Tine is to fork as
questions.explain: A tine is one of several identical prongs that make up a fork, and a spoke is one of several identical rods that make up a wheel. Wheel is to spoke gives the same link in reverse, whole first. Prong and tine are synonyms, cutlery is the category a fork belongs to, and axle is to rotate pairs a part with what it does.

questions.stem: Ventricle is to heart as lobe is to
questions.explain: A ventricle is one of the main chambers of the heart, and a lobe is one of the main divisions of the brain. A neuron is a cell within the brain, a smaller part rather than the whole. The spine is a separate structure connected to the brain, the skull is what encloses it and thought is what the brain produces.

questions.stem: Navigator is to sextant as surveyor is to
questions.explain: A navigator measures angles with a sextant, and a surveyor measures angles with a theodolite. A plat is the map a surveyor produces, a parcel is the land being surveyed and a boundary is what the survey marks, so each is a product or an object, not the tool. A cartographer is a related worker who makes maps.

questions.stem: Blacksmith is to anvil as
questions.explain: A blacksmith shapes metal on an anvil, and a potter shapes clay on a wheel, so each pair is a worker and the tool the work is formed on. A cobbler makes shoes (worker and product) and a baker works in a bakery (worker and place). Anvil is to forge pairs a tool with a workplace, and clay is to potter puts the material before the worker.

questions.stem: Carpenter is to plane as engraver is to
questions.explain: A carpenter uses a plane to shape wood, and an engraver uses a burin, a steel cutting tool, to cut lines into metal. An etching is a type of print, a plate is the material the engraver cuts and a studio is the workplace. Artisan is the broader category of skilled worker that includes engravers.

questions.stem: Whetstone is to sharpen as sieve is to
questions.explain: A whetstone is used to sharpen, and a sieve is used to sift. Knead is a baking action, but it is done with the hands, not a sieve. Mesh is the part of a sieve that does the work, flour is what is often sifted and a colander is a similar tool, so none of them is the action.

questions.stem: Altimeter is to altitude as tachometer is to
questions.explain: An altimeter measures altitude, and a tachometer measures rotational speed, such as engine or rotor revolutions per minute. Airspeed is shown by the airspeed indicator, torque by a torque meter and fuel flow by a fuel flow gauge, all instruments found near a tachometer on the panel. Distance flown is a calculation, not a tachometer reading.

questions.stem: Rasp is to abrade as
questions.explain: A rasp is a coarse file used to abrade (scrape away) a surface, and a scythe is a blade used to reap a crop, so each pair is a tool and the action it performs. Reap is to scythe reverses the order. Farmer is to scythe is a worker and a tool, plow is to field is a tool and the place it is used, and grain is to thresh is an object and an action done to it.

questions.stem: Deforestation is to erosion as
questions.explain: Deforestation causes soil erosion, and overfishing causes the depletion of fish stocks, so each pair runs from a human cause to its harmful effect. Starvation is to drought runs from effect to cause, the reverse. Irrigation is a remedy for aridity rather than its cause, a pasture is where livestock graze and topsoil is part of farmland.

questions.stem: Altitude is to hypoxia as acceleration is to
questions.explain: High altitude causes hypoxia (oxygen starvation), and high acceleration (G force) causes blackout, the loss of vision as blood drains from the head. Velocity is a related quantity, not an effect on the body. Thrust produces acceleration, so it is a cause, not an effect. A centrifuge is used to train for acceleration, and a G-suit is worn to prevent its effects.

questions.stem: Provocation is to retaliation as stimulus is to
questions.explain: A provocation produces retaliation, and a stimulus produces a response, so each pair is a prompt and the reaction it causes. Trigger and incentive are near synonyms of stimulus, so they repeat the cause instead of giving the effect. A nerve carries the signal, and a threshold is the level a stimulus must reach.

questions.stem: Cirrus is to cloud as sleet is to
questions.explain: Cirrus is one type of cloud, and sleet is one type of precipitation, so the second word is the category. Hail is another member of the same category, not the category itself. Cold is the condition sleet needs to form, a thunderstorm is an event that may produce precipitation and the atmosphere is where it forms.

questions.stem: Raptor is to falcon as
questions.explain: A falcon is a kind of raptor, and a dolphin is a kind of cetacean, so each pair runs from the category to one member. Dolphin is to cetacean reverses the order. A pod is a group of whales (a collective, not a category), a talon is part of a hawk and predator is to prey is a hunter and the hunted.

questions.stem: Basalt is to igneous as marble is to
questions.explain: Basalt is an igneous rock, and marble is a metamorphic rock, so the second word is the class of rock. Sedimentary is the trap: marble forms from limestone, which is sedimentary, but marble itself is metamorphic. Limestone is marble's parent rock, granite is another rock and a quarry is where marble is cut.

questions.stem: Aileron is to roll as rudder is to
questions.explain: The ailerons control an aircraft's roll, and the rudder controls its yaw, the movement of the nose left or right. Pitch is controlled by the elevator. Bank is the result of rolling, so it belongs to the ailerons. Lift comes from the wings and thrust from the engines.

questions.stem: Firebreak is to wildfire as
questions.explain: A firebreak exists to stop a wildfire from spreading, and a quarantine exists to stop a contagion from spreading. Contagion is to quarantine reverses the order. Arson causes a blaze rather than stopping it, a symptom is a sign of an infection, and an ember turns to ash, which is a sequence.

questions.stem: Splint is to fracture as tourniquet is to
questions.explain: A splint is used to treat a fracture, and a tourniquet is used to stop a hemorrhage (severe bleeding). A bandage is another first-aid item, not the condition it treats. Circulation is what a tourniquet cuts off, the limb is where it is placed and a paramedic is a person who applies it.

questions.stem: Cygnet is to swan as
questions.explain: A cygnet is a young swan that grows into an adult swan, and a leveret is a young hare that grows into an adult hare. Hare is to leveret reverses the order. A drake is a male duck, not a young one, a warren is where rabbits live and plumage is the feathering of a swan.

questions.stem: Takeoff is to climb as descent is to
questions.explain: In a flight, climb is the phase that follows takeoff, and approach is the phase that follows descent. Cruise comes before descent, so it reverses the order. Taxi happens on the ground before takeoff, altitude is a measurement and glide describes a way of descending, not the next phase.

questions.stem: Obdurate is to yielding as diffident is to
questions.explain: Obdurate (stubbornly unmoved) is the opposite of yielding, and diffident (shy, lacking confidence) is the opposite of assertive. Reticent and timid are synonyms of diffident. Indifferent is a sound-alike that means not caring, and obstinate is a synonym of obdurate from the first pair.

questions.stem: Pellucid is to murky as
questions.explain: Pellucid (perfectly clear) is the opposite of murky, and terse (brief) is the opposite of prolix (long-winded). Concise and succinct are synonyms. Dim to dark is a step up in degree, muddy describes a stream and an editor works on prose, so none of them is a pair of opposites.

questions.stem: Gregarious is to reclusive as magnanimous is to
questions.explain: Gregarious (sociable) is the opposite of reclusive, and magnanimous (generous in spirit, ready to forgive) is the opposite of petty. Generous and forgiving are close to synonyms of magnanimous. Majestic and grandiose play on the "magna" (great) in the word but are not its opposite.

questions.stem: Silo is to grain as
questions.explain: A silo is where grain is stored, and a magazine is where ammunition is stored. Ammunition is to magazine reverses the order. A trigger is part of a rifle, armory and arsenal are synonyms for a place that stores weapons, and a farmer grows a crop.

questions.stem: Monk is to monastery as nun is to
questions.explain: A monk lives in a monastery, and a nun lives in a convent, so the second word is the community where each lives. A chapel is a place of worship, not a dwelling. A habit is what a nun wears, an abbess is the nun who heads a convent and a vow is the promise a nun makes.

questions.stem: Linen is to flax as burlap is to
questions.explain: Linen is a fabric woven from the fibers of the flax plant, and burlap is a fabric woven from the fibers of the jute plant. Cotton is the source of other fabrics, and canvas is another coarse fabric, not a raw material. A sack is made from burlap, and a loom is the machine that weaves it.

questions.stem: Honey is to nectar as
questions.explain: Honey is made from nectar, and cheese is made from milk, so each pair is a product and its raw material. Milk is to cheese reverses the order. A cow produces milk, which pairs an animal with its product, butter is made in a churn (product and equipment), and cheddar is a kind of cheese.

questions.stem: Callow is to experience as listless is to
questions.explain: Callow means lacking experience, and listless means lacking energy. Fatigue is what a listless person feels, so it is something present, not absent. Order is a trap based on the word "list." Courage and memory are qualities that other words (cowardly, forgetful) describe a lack of.

questions.stem: Impecunious is to money as
questions.explain: Impecunious means having no money, and ignorant means having no knowledge. Learned and affluent describe having plenty of knowledge and wealth, the opposite relationship. A miser hoards gold, and penury and poverty are synonyms.

questions.stem: Intrepid is to fear as candid is to
questions.explain: An intrepid person is without fear, and a candid person is without guile (cunning or deceit). Candor and honesty are qualities a candid person has, not ones they lack. Speech is how candor is shown, and courage belongs to the first pair, since it is what an intrepid person has.

questions.stem: Skull and crossbones is to poison as
questions.explain: A skull and crossbones is the symbol that stands for poison, and a pair of scales is the symbol that stands for justice. Justice is to scales reverses the order. A judge works in a courtroom, a verdict is the outcome of a trial and an antidote counteracts a poison.

questions.stem: Phoenix is to rebirth as poppy is to
questions.explain: The phoenix, which rises from its own ashes, symbolizes rebirth, and the red poppy, worn for those killed in war, symbolizes remembrance. Opium is a product made from a kind of poppy, not what the flower stands for. Flanders is the region whose battlefields made the poppy a symbol, a petal is part of the flower and crimson is its color.

questions.stem: Recalcitrant is to defiant as perfidious is to
questions.explain: Recalcitrant and defiant are synonyms, and perfidious (deceitful, untrustworthy) and treacherous are synonyms. Perfunctory (done with little care), perilous (dangerous) and pernicious (harmful) share the "per" sound but have different meanings. Loyal is the opposite of perfidious.

questions.stem: Abate is to subside as
questions.explain: Abate and subside are synonyms, and augment and increase are synonyms. Wax and wane are opposites. Diminish is to vanish is a step up in degree, quell is to riot is an action and what it is done to, and storm is to abate is a thing and what it does.

questions.stem: Chameleon is to changeable as mule is to
questions.explain: A chameleon is proverbially changeable, and a mule is proverbially stubborn, so the second word is the trait each animal is known for. Docile is close to the opposite of that trait. Timid and swift are not traits associated with mules, and burdened describes the loads a mule carries rather than its nature.

questions.stem: Sycophant is to obsequious as
questions.explain: A sycophant is by definition obsequious (excessively eager to please), and a braggart is by definition boastful, so each pair is a type of person and the trait that defines them. Boastful is to braggart reverses the order. A miser is the opposite of generous, a hermit avoids a crowd and a critic writes a review.

questions.stem: Zealot is to fervent as skeptic is to
questions.explain: A zealot is characteristically fervent, and a skeptic is characteristically incredulous (unwilling to believe). Credulous looks similar but means the opposite, ready to believe anything. Devout and zealous describe the zealot from the first pair, and heretical means holding views against accepted doctrine, which is not the same as doubting.

questions.stem: A transport aircraft cruises at a true airspeed of 250 knots. It flies 600 nautical miles straight into a steady 50-knot headwind, then flies the same 600 nautical miles back with that wind behind it. What is its average ground speed for the whole round trip?
questions.explain: Outbound ground speed is 250 - 50 = 200 knots, so that leg takes 600 / 200 = 3 hours; inbound is 250 + 50 = 300 knots, taking 600 / 300 = 2 hours. Average speed = total distance / total time = 1,200 / 5 = 240 knots. Check: 240 x 5 = 1,200. 250 averages the two speeds instead of using total time, 200 and 300 are single legs, and 120 forgets the trip covers 1,200 nautical miles, not 600.

questions.stem: Two aircraft are 1,320 nautical miles apart on the same airway, flying toward each other. One departs at 1300 at 240 knots; the other departs at 1330 at 360 knots. At what time do they pass each other?
questions.explain: By 1330 the first aircraft has flown 240 x 0.5 = 120 nautical miles, leaving 1,320 - 120 = 1,200. From then they close at 240 + 360 = 600 knots, so they meet 1,200 / 600 = 2 hours after 1330, at 1530. Check: first aircraft flies 2.5 h x 240 = 600, second 2 h x 360 = 720, total 1,320. 1512 treats both as leaving at 1300, 1500 adds the 2 hours to 1300, 1542 adds 2 h 12 min to 1330, and 1545 wrongly assumes they meet at the halfway point.

questions.stem: A jet burns 2,400 pounds of fuel per hour and has 16,800 pounds of usable fuel. It must land with a 45-minute fuel reserve. At a ground speed of 420 knots, what is the greatest distance it can fly before landing?
questions.explain: The reserve is 0.75 h x 2,400 = 1,800 pounds, leaving 16,800 - 1,800 = 15,000 pounds to fly on. That is 15,000 / 2,400 = 6.25 hours, and 6.25 x 420 = 2,625 nautical miles. Check: 6.25 h + 0.75 h = 7 h, which is all 16,800 pounds. 2,940 ignores the reserve, 2,520 and 2,730 use 1-hour and 30-minute reserves, and 2,695 misreads 6.25 hours as 6 hours 25 minutes.

questions.stem: One maintenance crew can complete an engine inspection in 6 hours; a second crew can complete the same inspection in 3 hours. The first crew works alone for 2 hours, then both crews work together to finish. How long does the whole inspection take from the start?
questions.explain: In 2 hours the first crew does 2/6 = 1/3 of the job, leaving 2/3. Together they work at 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 job per hour, so the rest takes (2/3) / (1/2) = 4/3 hours = 1 hour 20 minutes, for a total of 3 hours 20 minutes. Check: crew 1 does 3 1/3 h x 1/6 = 5/9 and crew 2 does 4/3 h x 1/3 = 4/9, which adds to 1. 3 h 33 min misreads 1.33 hours as 1 h 33 min, 4 hours redoes the whole job together after 2 hours, 2 hours assumes both worked from the start, and 1 h 20 min leaves out the first 2 hours.

questions.stem: A base's quarterly travel budget of $40,000 is cut by 25 percent. The next quarter, the reduced budget is increased by 20 percent. What is the budget after both changes?
questions.explain: After the cut the budget is $40,000 x 0.75 = $30,000. A 20 percent rise on that amount gives $30,000 x 1.20 = $36,000. Check: the net multiplier is 0.75 x 1.20 = 0.90, a 10 percent drop. $38,000 just nets the percents (-25 + 20 = -5 percent), $30,000 stops after the cut, $48,000 applies the 20 percent rise to the original, and $24,000 treats the rise as a second cut.

questions.stem: In a squadron the ratio of pilots to combat systems officers is 5:3, and the ratio of combat systems officers to enlisted aircrew is 2:7. If there are 60 pilots, how many enlisted aircrew are there?
questions.explain: With 60 pilots, combat systems officers = 60 x 3/5 = 36. Enlisted aircrew = 36 x 7/2 = 126. Check: the combined ratio is 10:6:21, and 60/10 = 6, so 6 x 21 = 126. 84 wrongly chains the ratios as 5:3:7, 140 applies 7/3 to the pilots, 210 treats the 60 pilots as the 2 in the second ratio, and 36 stops at the officer count.

questions.stem: On a chart where 1 inch represents 8 nautical miles, a route has three legs measuring 2 1/4 inches, 3 1/2 inches, and 1 3/4 inches. How many minutes will it take an aircraft flying at a ground speed of 120 knots to fly the route?
questions.explain: The legs total 2.25 + 3.5 + 1.75 = 7.5 inches, which is 7.5 x 8 = 60 nautical miles. At 120 knots that takes 60 / 120 = 0.5 hour = 30 minutes. Check: 120 knots is 2 nautical miles per minute, and 60 / 2 = 30. 50 minutes misreads 0.5 hour as 50 minutes, 28 and 32 come from adding the legs to 7 or 8 inches, and 60 reports the distance as if the aircraft flew 1 nautical mile per minute.

questions.stem: A student pilot's first four checkride scores average 82. What score on the fifth checkride would raise the overall average to exactly 85?
questions.explain: The first four scores total 4 x 82 = 328. An average of 85 over five rides needs 5 x 85 = 425 points, so the fifth score must be 425 - 328 = 97. Check: the fifth score must make up 3 points for each of the four earlier rides (12) on top of 85. 88 adds the 3-point gap only once, 94 makes up the gap for only three rides, 100 adds 3 for all five rides, and 91 doubles the gap.

questions.stem: A wing has three squadrons. Squadron A has 20 members with an average fitness score of 90, Squadron B has 30 members averaging 85, and Squadron C has 50 members averaging 80. What is the average score of all members in the wing?
questions.explain: Total points = 20 x 90 + 30 x 85 + 50 x 80 = 1,800 + 2,550 + 4,000 = 8,350. Dividing by 100 members gives 83.5. Check: the answer sits closer to 80 because C is the largest squadron. 85.0 is the plain average of the three squadron averages, 86.5 pairs the 50 members with 90 instead of 80, 82.5 averages only B and C, and 87.5 averages only A and B.

questions.stem: A tank holds 400 gallons of fuel blend that is 10 percent additive. How many gallons of pure additive must be added to make the blend 20 percent additive?
questions.explain: The tank has 0.10 x 400 = 40 gallons of additive. Adding x gallons of pure additive: 40 + x = 0.20(400 + x), so 40 + x = 80 + 0.2x, 0.8x = 40, and x = 50. Check: 90 / 450 = 20 percent. 40 forgets the added additive also increases the total volume, 80 is 20 percent of 400, 200 divides 40 by 0.20, and 100 would give 140 / 500 = 28 percent.

questions.stem: A lieutenant deposits $6,000 in an account paying 4 percent simple annual interest. How much is in the account after 2 years and 6 months?
questions.explain: 2 years 6 months is 2.5 years. Interest = 6,000 x 0.04 x 2.5 = $600, so the balance is 6,000 + 600 = $6,600. Check: one year earns $240, and 2.5 x 240 = 600. $6,480 uses 2 years, $6,720 uses 3 years, $600 is the interest alone, and $6,624 treats 2 years 6 months as 2.6 years.

questions.stem: An officer invests $5,000 at 10 percent interest compounded annually. How much more interest does she earn in the third year than in the first year?
questions.explain: Year 1 interest is 10 percent of $5,000 = $500, making $5,500. Year 2 interest is $550, making $6,050. Year 3 interest is $605, and 605 - 500 = $105. Check: $6,655 at the end is 5,000 x 1.1 x 1.1 x 1.1. $50 is the year 2 minus year 1 gap, $100 doubles that gap as if growth were linear, $605 is the third-year interest itself, and $1,655 is the total interest for all three years.

questions.stem: An aircraft's ground speed is 360 knots. About how many statute miles does it cover in 25 minutes? (1 nautical mile = 1.15 statute miles)
questions.explain: 360 knots is 6 nautical miles per minute, so 25 minutes covers 6 x 25 = 150 nautical miles. Converting, 150 x 1.15 = 172.5 statute miles. Check: statute miles must be the larger number. 150.0 skips the conversion, 103.5 treats 25 minutes as 0.25 hour, 207.0 uses 30 minutes, and 130.4 divides by 1.15 instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: A rectangular fuel bladder is 12 feet long, 8 feet wide, and 4 feet deep. If it is filled to three-quarters of its depth, how many gallons does it hold? (1 cubic foot = 7.5 gallons)
questions.explain: Three-quarters of 4 feet is 3 feet, so the fuel volume is 12 x 8 x 3 = 288 cubic feet. Converting, 288 x 7.5 = 2,160 gallons. Check: the full bladder is 384 cubic feet, or 2,880 gallons, and 3/4 of 2,880 is 2,160. 2,880 is the full bladder, 720 uses one-quarter depth, 288 leaves the answer in cubic feet, and 38.4 divides by 7.5.

questions.stem: A detachment orders 14 meal kits at $9.50 each and 6 cases of water at $4.25 each. A 10 percent discount is applied to the whole order. What is the final cost?
questions.explain: Meal kits cost 14 x 9.50 = $133.00 and water costs 6 x 4.25 = $25.50, for $158.50. A 10 percent discount leaves 158.50 x 0.90 = $142.65. Check: 158.50 - 15.85 = 142.65. $158.50 ignores the discount, $145.20 discounts only the meal kits, $155.95 discounts only the water, and $15.85 is the discount itself.

questions.stem: A colonel is now three times as old as her son. In 12 years she will be twice as old as her son will be then. How old is the colonel now?
questions.explain: Let the son be s, so the colonel is 3s. In 12 years: 3s + 12 = 2(s + 12) = 2s + 24, so s = 12 and the colonel is 36. Check: in 12 years they are 48 and 24, and 48 is twice 24. 12 is the son's age, 48 and 24 are their ages in 12 years, and 72 forgets to add 12 years to the colonel's age (3s = 2(s + 12)).

questions.stem: A C-17 departs Dover AFB, Delaware (Eastern Time) at 2200 local time and flies 8 hours 30 minutes to Ramstein AB, Germany, which is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Time. What is the local time at Ramstein when it lands?
questions.explain: Departure at 2200 Eastern is 2200 + 6 = 0400 the next morning in Germany. Adding the 8 hours 30 minutes flight gives 1230 Ramstein time. Check: landing is 0630 Eastern, and 0630 + 6 hours = 1230. 0630 is the Eastern arrival time with no zone change, 0030 subtracts the 6 hours, 1130 is an hour short, and 1218 treats 8 h 30 min as 8.3 hours (8 h 18 min).

questions.stem: A tanker departs at 0900 flying at 300 knots. A fighter departs the same base at 0930 on the same track at 450 knots to join it. At what time does the fighter catch the tanker?
questions.explain: By 0930 the tanker is 300 x 0.5 = 150 nautical miles ahead. The fighter gains 450 - 300 = 150 knots, so it closes the gap in 150 / 150 = 1 hour, at 1030. Check: at 1030 the tanker has flown 1.5 x 300 = 450 and the fighter 1 x 450 = 450. 1000 counts the hour from 0900, 0942 adds the speeds instead of subtracting, 1130 uses a full hour's head start, and 0950 divides the gap by the fighter's speed.

questions.stem: A helicopter burns 90 gallons of fuel per hour. Its fuel weighs 6.8 pounds per gallon. How many pounds of fuel does it burn on a flight of 2 hours 20 minutes?
questions.explain: 2 hours 20 minutes is 2 1/3 hours, so it burns 90 x 7/3 = 210 gallons. At 6.8 pounds per gallon that is 210 x 6.8 = 1,428 pounds. Check: 200 x 6.8 = 1,360 plus 10 x 6.8 = 68 gives 1,428. 1,224 uses 2 hours only, 1,346.4 treats 2 h 20 min as 2.2 hours, 210 leaves the answer in gallons, and 1,530 uses 2.5 hours.

questions.stem: A fuel truck's pump can fill an empty storage tank in 40 minutes. A leak in the tank would drain a full tank in 2 hours. With the leak present the whole time, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explain: The pump fills 1/40 of the tank per minute and the leak drains 1/120 per minute. Net rate = 1/40 - 1/120 = 3/120 - 1/120 = 2/120 = 1/60, so it takes 60 minutes. Check: in 60 minutes the pump adds 1.5 tanks and the leak removes 0.5 tank. 30 adds the leak rate instead of subtracting it, 80 averages 40 and 120, 160 adds the two times, and 120 is just the leak's time.

questions.stem: A squadron flew 1,250 sorties last year and 1,000 sorties this year. By what percent must next year's total rise above this year's to get back to last year's level?
questions.explain: The squadron needs 1,250 - 1,000 = 250 more sorties. Measured against this year's 1,000, that is 250 / 1,000 = 25 percent. Check: 1,000 x 1.25 = 1,250. 20 percent divides by last year's 1,250 (that is the size of the drop, not the needed rise), 80 percent is 1,000 / 1,250, 125 percent is the ratio 1,250 / 1,000 rather than the increase, and 22.5 percent averages the two bases.

questions.stem: A flight jacket is marked $240. It is reduced 25 percent, a military coupon then takes 10 percent off the sale price, and 5 percent sales tax is charged on the final price. What does the jacket cost?
questions.explain: After the 25 percent cut: 240 x 0.75 = $180. After the coupon: 180 x 0.90 = $162. With tax: 162 x 1.05 = $170.10. Check: 162 + 8.10 = 170.10. $163.80 takes a single 35 percent off before tax, $162.00 leaves out the tax, $144.00 treats the tax as another 5 percent discount, and $189.00 forgets the coupon.

questions.stem: A ground crew of 6 airmen can load 18 pallets in 45 minutes. At the same rate per airman, how many minutes will a crew of 9 need to load 36 pallets?
questions.explain: Twice as many pallets doubles the time to 90 minutes for 6 airmen. Using 9 airmen instead of 6 divides the time by 1.5, so 90 / 1.5 = 60 minutes. Check: 6 airmen x 45 min = 270 airman-minutes per 18 pallets, so 36 pallets need 540, and 540 / 9 = 60. 90 ignores the larger crew, 30 ignores the doubled load, 135 multiplies by 1.5 instead of dividing, and 67.5 does that while also ignoring the doubled load.

questions.stem: An aircraft climbs from 4,500 feet to 18,000 feet at 1,800 feet per minute, then from 18,000 feet to 31,500 feet at 1,200 feet per minute. How long does the whole climb take?
questions.explain: The first segment is 13,500 feet at 1,800 ft/min = 7.5 minutes. The second segment is also 13,500 feet, at 1,200 ft/min = 11.25 minutes. Total = 18.75 minutes = 18 minutes 45 seconds. Check: 7.5 x 1,800 + 11.25 x 1,200 = 13,500 + 13,500 = 27,000 feet. 18 minutes averages the two rates, 15 and 22 min 30 s use one rate for the whole climb, and 21 min 15 s starts the climb from 0 feet.

questions.stem: A rectangular aircraft parking apron is 300 feet by 240 feet. A taxi lane 20 feet wide runs along the inside of the entire perimeter and cannot be used for parking. How many square feet are left for parking?
questions.explain: The lane takes 20 feet off each side, so the parking area is (300 - 40) by (240 - 40) = 260 by 200 = 52,000 square feet. Check: total 72,000 minus lane 20,000 = 52,000. 61,600 removes the lane from only one side in each direction, 50,400 subtracts perimeter x 20 and so counts the four corners twice, 20,000 is the lane itself, and 72,000 is the whole apron.

questions.stem: The sum of three consecutive even integers is 78 more than the smallest of them. What is the largest of the three?
questions.explain: Let the integers be n, n + 2, and n + 4. Their sum 3n + 6 equals n + 78, so 2n = 72 and n = 36, making the largest 40. Check: 36 + 38 + 40 = 114, and 114 - 36 = 78. 36 and 38 are the smallest and middle numbers, while 26 and 30 come from treating 78 as the whole sum (78 / 3 = 26, then adding 4).

questions.stem: A remotely piloted aircraft launches at 1340 and flies 156 nautical miles at 72 knots. At what time does it reach its destination?
questions.explain: 72 knots is 72 / 60 = 1.2 nautical miles per minute, so 156 nautical miles takes 156 / 1.2 = 130 minutes = 2 hours 10 minutes. 1340 + 2:10 = 1550. Check: 2 1/6 hours x 72 = 144 + 12 = 156. 1557 reads 2.17 hours as 2 h 17 min, 1540 drops the 10 minutes, 1600 rounds the time up to 2 h 20 min, and 1647 multiplies 156 by 1.2 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: A patrol aircraft flies 360 nautical miles at 180 knots and then 720 nautical miles at 240 knots. What is its average speed for the whole flight?
questions.explain: The first leg takes 360 / 180 = 2 hours and the second 720 / 240 = 3 hours. Average speed = 1,080 / 5 = 216 knots. Check: 216 x 5 = 1,080. 210 is the plain average of the two speeds, 220 weights the speeds by distance instead of time, 206 uses the equal-distance formula (2 x 180 x 240 / 420), and 240 is only the second leg's speed.

questions.stem: A dining facility blends coffee costing $6 per pound with 30 pounds of coffee costing $10 per pound. How many pounds of the $6 coffee are needed so the blend is worth $7 per pound?
questions.explain: Set total value equal: 6x + 10(30) = 7(x + 30), so 6x + 300 = 7x + 210 and x = 90. Check: 90 x 6 + 300 = 840, and 840 / 120 = $7. 10 reverses the 3:1 cheap-to-expensive ratio, 30 (equal amounts) would give $8 per pound, 60 is a near miss giving $7.33, and 120 is the total weight of the blend.

questions.stem: On a map, 1.5 inches represents 20 miles. A rectangular training range measures 4.5 inches by 3 inches on the map. What is the range's actual area?
questions.explain: 4.5 inches is 3 x 1.5 inches = 60 miles, and 3 inches is 2 x 1.5 inches = 40 miles. Area = 60 x 40 = 2,400 square miles. Check: the map area is 13.5 square inches and each square inch covers (40/3)^2, about 177.8 square miles, which gives 2,400. 180 scales the map area by the linear factor only, 5,400 uses 1 inch = 20 miles, 200 is the perimeter, and 12,150 uses 1 inch = 30 miles.

questions.stem: Of 80 pilot candidates, 75 percent passed the first phase of training. Of those who passed, 60 percent passed the second phase. What percent of the original 80 failed at least one phase?
questions.explain: 75 percent of 80 = 60 passed phase one, and 60 percent of 60 = 36 passed both. So 80 - 36 = 44 failed at least one phase, and 44 / 80 = 55 percent. Check: 0.75 x 0.60 = 0.45 passed both, and 1 - 0.45 = 0.55. 45 percent is the share that passed both, 65 percent adds 25 and 40 as if both were out of the whole class, 40 percent is the phase-two failure rate among those who took it, and 25 percent counts only phase-one failures.

questions.stem: A mission briefing starts at 1945 and lasts 2 hours 50 minutes. The crew must be at the aircraft 1 hour 25 minutes after the briefing ends. At what time must they be at the aircraft?
questions.explain: 1945 + 2 h 50 min = 2235. 2235 + 1 h 25 min = 2400, which is written 0000. Check: the total added time is 4 h 15 min, and 1945 + 4:15 = 2400. 2235 is when the briefing ends, 2320 adds the times as decimals (1945 + 250 + 125), 2330 turns 2:50 + 1:25 into 3:75 and reads it as 3.75 hours, and 0015 is 15 minutes too late.

questions.stem: An aircraft has 4 hours of usable fuel and a true airspeed of 200 knots. It flies out into a 40-knot headwind and must return to base on the same route with no reserve. How far out can it fly before it must turn back?
questions.explain: Ground speed out is 160 knots and back is 240 knots. For distance d: d/160 + d/240 = 4, so (3d + 2d)/480 = 4, 5d = 1,920, and d = 384 nautical miles. Check: 384/160 = 2.4 h and 384/240 = 1.6 h, total 4 h. 400 splits the time equally and ignores the wind, 320 and 480 split the time equally at one ground speed, and 768 is the total distance out and back.

questions.stem: Three technicians can rewire an avionics panel alone in 4 hours, 6 hours, and 12 hours. How long will the job take if all three work together?
questions.explain: Their hourly rates are 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 + 2/12 + 1/12 = 6/12 = 1/2 job per hour, so the job takes 2 hours. Check: in 2 hours they finish 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1 job. 7 h 20 min averages the three times, 2 h 27 min divides that average by 3, 22 hours adds the times, and 4 hours is the fastest technician alone, which teamwork must beat.

questions.stem: A unit buys 250 headsets at $80 each. It sells 40 percent of them to another unit at a 15 percent markup and the rest at cost. What is the total amount it receives?
questions.explain: 40 percent of 250 is 100 headsets sold at 80 x 1.15 = $92, bringing in $9,200. The other 150 sell at $80 for $12,000. Total = $21,200. Check: cost $20,000 plus markup 100 x $12 = $1,200. $20,000 sells everything at cost, $23,000 marks up every headset, $21,800 marks up 60 percent instead of 40 percent, and $1,200 is only the markup.

questions.stem: A receiver aircraft needs 40,500 pounds of fuel. The tanker's boom transfers 900 gallons per minute, and the fuel weighs 6.75 pounds per gallon. How long does the transfer take?
questions.explain: 40,500 pounds / 6.75 pounds per gallon = 6,000 gallons. At 900 gallons per minute that is 6,000 / 900 = 6 2/3 minutes = 6 minutes 40 seconds. Check: 900 x 6.75 = 6,075 pounds per minute, and 6,075 x 6 2/3 = 40,500. 45 minutes skips the pounds-to-gallons step, 7 min 30 s uses 6 pounds per gallon, 6 minutes uses 7.5 pounds per gallon, and about 304 minutes multiplies by 6.75 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: An eastbound convoy leaves a depot at 0800 at 40 mph. A westbound convoy leaves the same depot at 0930 at 60 mph. At what time will the two convoys be 360 miles apart?
questions.explain: By 0930 the eastbound convoy has a 1.5-hour head start of 40 x 1.5 = 60 miles. After that the gap grows at 40 + 60 = 100 mph, so the remaining 300 miles take 3 hours, and 0930 + 3 h = 1230. 1136 treats both convoys as leaving at 0800 (360 / 100 = 3.6 h), 1306 ignores the head start and runs 3.6 h from 0930, 1100 adds the correct 3 hours to 0800 instead of 0930, and 1212 works out the head start at the westbound 60 mph.

questions.stem: A number is increased by 20 percent, and the result is then decreased by 20 percent. The final value is 12 less than the original number. What was the original number?
questions.explain: The two changes multiply: 1.20 x 0.80 = 0.96, so the final value is 96 percent of the original. The loss of 4 percent equals 12, so the original is 12 / 0.04 = 300. Check: 300 rises to 360, then falls to 288, which is 12 less. 288 is the final value, 60 divides 12 by 0.20, 600 treats the loss as 2 percent, and 150 treats it as 8 percent.

questions.stem: A borrower repays a $4,500 simple-interest loan after 3 years with a single payment of $5,310. At the same annual rate, how much simple interest would a $6,000 loan accrue in 2 years?
questions.explain: Interest on the first loan is 5,310 − 4,500 = $810, or 810 / 3 = $270 a year, and 270 / 4,500 = 0.06, so the rate is 6 percent. On $6,000 for 2 years the interest is 6,000 x 0.06 x 2 = $720. $1,080 uses 3 years instead of 2, $540 scales the $810 for the shorter time but not the larger principal, $2,160 uses 18 percent by forgetting to divide by the 3 years, and $6,720 is the total owed rather than the interest.

questions.stem: A recruiting office's applications rose 10 percent in each of three consecutive years, reaching 1,331. How many applications did it receive before the first increase?
questions.explain: Three 10 percent rises multiply the starting number by 1.1 x 1.1 x 1.1 = 1.331. So the start was 1,331 / 1.331 = 1,000. Check: 1,000 to 1,100 to 1,210 to 1,331. 1,024 divides by 1.3 (adding the percents), 932 takes 30 percent off 1,331, 970 takes 10 percent off three times, and 1,210 undoes only one year.

questions.stem: An award of $3,600 is split among three airmen in the ratio 2:3:4. How much more does the airman with the largest share receive than the airman with the smallest share?
questions.explain: The ratio has 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts, so one part is 3,600 / 9 = $400. The shares are $800, $1,200, and $1,600, and the difference is 1,600 - 800 = $800. Check: 800 + 1,200 + 1,600 = 3,600. $400 is one part, $1,600 is the largest share, $1,200 is the middle share, and $2,400 divides by 3 people instead of 9 parts.

questions.stem: An aircraft flies 420 nautical miles from base A to base B with a 30-knot tailwind in 1 hour 45 minutes. It returns along the same route with the same wind, now a headwind. How long does the return flight take?
questions.explain: Outbound ground speed = 420 / 1.75 = 240 knots, so the true airspeed is 240 - 30 = 210 knots. Into the wind the ground speed is 210 - 30 = 180 knots, and 420 / 180 = 2 1/3 hours = 2 hours 20 minutes. Check: 180 x 7/3 = 420. 2 hours treats 240 as the airspeed and subtracts the wind once, 2 h 33 min misreads 2.33 hours, 1 h 45 min ignores the wind, and 2 h 30 min is a near miss with no valid working behind it.

questions.stem: A cylindrical water tank has a diameter of 14 feet and a height of 10 feet. How many gallons does it hold when full? (Use pi = 22/7 and 1 cubic foot = 7.5 gallons.)
questions.explain: The radius is 14 / 2 = 7 feet. Volume = (22/7) x 7 x 7 x 10 = 22 x 7 x 10 = 1,540 cubic feet, and 1,540 x 7.5 = 11,550 gallons. Check: 1,540 x 7 = 10,780 plus 1,540 x 0.5 = 770 gives 11,550. 46,200 uses the diameter as the radius, 1,540 is still in cubic feet, 3,300 uses the side area 2 pi r h, and 23,100 multiplies the diameter by the radius instead of squaring the radius.

questions.stem: A course grade is weighted 30 percent written exam, 50 percent simulator, and 20 percent flight evaluation. A student scores 80 on the written exam and 90 in the simulator. What flight evaluation score does she need for a course grade of 88?
questions.explain: The written exam contributes 0.30 x 80 = 24 and the simulator 0.50 x 90 = 45, for 69 points. She needs 88 - 69 = 19 more points from 0.20 x F, so F = 19 / 0.20 = 95. Check: 24 + 45 + 0.20 x 95 = 24 + 45 + 19 = 88. 94 treats the three parts as equally weighted, 19 forgets to divide by 0.20, 105 swaps the written and simulator weights, and 100 overshoots to a 89 course grade.

questions.stem: A crew departs Hickam, Hawaii (UTC-10) at 2300 local time on January 3 and flies 7 hours 30 minutes to Guam (UTC+10). What is the local date and time in Guam on arrival?
questions.explain: 2300 on January 3 in Hawaii is 0900 UTC on January 4. Adding the flight gives 1630 UTC on January 4, and Guam is 10 hours ahead of UTC, so it is 0230 on January 5. Check: Guam is 20 hours ahead of Hawaii, and Hawaii arrival time 0630 January 4 plus 20 hours is 0230 January 5. 0230 January 4 drops the date change, 0630 January 4 is Hawaii time, 1030 January 3 subtracts the 20 hours, and 1630 January 4 is UTC.

questions.stem: A vehicle rental costs $45 per day plus $0.25 per mile for every mile over 200 for the whole rental. A team rents a vehicle for 4 days and drives 620 miles. What is the total cost?
questions.explain: The daily charge is 4 x 45 = $180. The chargeable mileage is 620 - 200 = 420 miles, costing 420 x 0.25 = $105. Total = 180 + 105 = $285. Check: $335 - $285 = $50, which is the cost of the 200 free miles. $335 charges all 620 miles, $180 applies 200 free miles per day (so no mileage charge), $150 charges only one day, and $105 is the mileage charge alone.

questions.stem: Twelve airmen can fill 900 sandbags in 5 hours. Working at the same rate, how many additional airmen are needed to fill 1,350 sandbags in 3 hours?
questions.explain: Each airman fills 900 / (12 x 5) = 15 sandbags per hour. To fill 1,350 in 3 hours needs 1,350 / 3 = 450 per hour, or 450 / 15 = 30 airmen, so 30 - 12 = 18 more are needed. Check: 30 x 15 x 3 = 1,350. 30 is the total crew, not the extra airmen, 6 ignores the shorter time, 8 ignores the larger number of bags, and 12 just doubles the crew.

questions.stem: A 60-gallon tank of de-icing fluid is 40 percent glycol. How many gallons must be drained and replaced with pure glycol to make the tank 60 percent glycol?
questions.explain: The tank has 0.40 x 60 = 24 gallons of glycol and needs 0.60 x 60 = 36. Draining x gallons removes 0.4x glycol, and adding x pure glycol adds x, so the net gain is 0.6x = 12 and x = 20. Check: 24 - 8 + 20 = 36, and 36 / 60 = 60 percent. 12 ignores the glycol lost in the drained fluid, 30 adds pure glycol without draining (the tank grows to 90 gallons), and 24 and 15 do not give 60 percent (24 gives 64 percent, 15 gives 55 percent).

questions.stem: The digits of a two-digit number add up to 11. When the digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original. What is the original number?
questions.explain: Write the number as 10a + b. Reversing gives 10b + a, and the difference is 9(b - a) = 27, so b - a = 3. With a + b = 11, b = 7 and a = 4, so the number is 47. Check: 74 - 47 = 27 and 4 + 7 = 11. 74 is the reversed number, and 38, 56, and 29 have digits that add to 11 but reverse to gains of 45, 9, and 63.

questions.stem: A ground support vehicle travels 168 miles on 12 gallons of fuel. Fuel costs $3.50 per gallon. What is the fuel cost for a 490-mile trip?
questions.explain: The vehicle gets 168 / 12 = 14 miles per gallon, so 490 miles needs 490 / 14 = 35 gallons. At $3.50 per gallon that costs 35 x 3.50 = $122.50. Check: $42 buys 12 gallons for 168 miles, and 490 is 35/12 of that distance. $42.00 is the cost of the original 168 miles, $140.00 divides 490 by 3.50, $1,715.00 multiplies 490 by 3.50, and $35.00 reports the gallons as dollars.

questions.stem: After a 15 percent reduction, a squadron's annual flight-hour allocation is 3,400 hours. What was the allocation before the reduction?
questions.explain: 3,400 hours is 85 percent of the original, so the original was 3,400 / 0.85 = 4,000 hours. Check: 15 percent of 4,000 is 600, and 4,000 - 600 = 3,400. 3,910 adds 15 percent of 3,400 (the wrong base), 2,890 takes another 15 percent off, 510 is 15 percent of 3,400, and 22,667 divides by 0.15 instead of 0.85.

questions.stem: A drone flies at 180 knots. What is its speed in feet per second? (1 nautical mile = 6,080 feet)
questions.topic: Unit conversion (knots to feet per second)
questions.explain: 180 knots is 180 x 6,080 = 1,094,400 feet per hour. Dividing by 3,600 seconds per hour gives 304 feet per second. Check: 180 / 3,600 = 1/20 nautical mile per second, and 6,080 / 20 = 304. 264 uses 5,280 feet (a statute mile), 18,240 is feet per minute, 30.4 misplaces the decimal, and 1,094,400 is feet per hour.

questions.stem: A hangar floor 120 feet by 80 feet needs two coats of sealant. One gallon covers 400 square feet, and the sealant is sold only in 5-gallon pails at $170 per pail. What is the least it can cost to buy enough sealant?
questions.explain: The floor is 120 x 80 = 9,600 square feet, so two coats cover 19,200 square feet and need 19,200 / 400 = 48 gallons. 48 / 5 = 9.6, so 10 whole pails are required, costing 10 x 170 = $1,700. Check: 10 pails give 50 gallons, covering 20,000 square feet. $850 is one coat, $1,728 prices gallons singly at $36, $1,530 rounds down to 9 pails (only 45 gallons), and $1,632 pays for 9.6 pails, which cannot be bought.

questions.stem: The ages of a pilot and her daughter add up to 48. Six years ago, the pilot was five times as old as her daughter. How old is the daughter now?
questions.explain: Let the daughter be d, so the pilot is 48 - d. Six years ago: 48 - d - 6 = 5(d - 6), so 42 - d = 5d - 30, 72 = 6d, and d = 12. Check: six years ago they were 30 and 6, and 30 = 5 x 6. 36 is the pilot's age, 6 and 30 are their ages six years ago, and 8 ignores the six years (48 / 6).

questions.stem: A fuel contract price rises 20 percent in January and another 10 percent in June, then falls 25 percent in December. What is the net change from the original price?
questions.explain: Multiply the factors: 1.20 x 1.10 = 1.32, and 1.32 x 0.75 = 0.99, which is 1 percent below the original. Check with $100: $120, then $132, then $132 - $33 = $99. 5 percent increase adds the percents (20 + 10 - 25), 2.5 percent decrease adds the two rises to 30 percent before multiplying, 7 percent increase takes the 25 percent off the original price, and no change assumes the rises and the fall cancel out.

questions.stem: A scale model of an aircraft is built at a scale of 1:72. The real aircraft has a wingspan of 108 feet. What is the model's wingspan in inches?
questions.explain: The model wingspan is 108 / 72 = 1.5 feet. Converting to inches, 1.5 x 12 = 18 inches. Check: 18 inches x 72 = 1,296 inches, and 1,296 / 12 = 108 feet. 1.5 forgets to convert feet to inches, 15 misreads 1.5 feet as 15 inches, 9 divides 108 by 12 instead of by 72, and 6 divides 72 by 12.

questions.stem: A unit buys 40 parts at $12 each and then 60 more at $15 each. It resells all 100 parts at 20 percent above their average cost. What is the selling price per part?
questions.explain: Total cost = 40 x 12 + 60 x 15 = 480 + 900 = $1,380, so the average cost is $13.80. Adding 20 percent gives 13.80 x 1.20 = $16.56. Check: 13.80 + 2.76 = 16.56. $16.20 marks up the simple average $13.50, $13.80 is the cost with no markup, $15.84 swaps the quantities (40 at $15, 60 at $12), and $2.76 is only the markup.

questions.stem: A courier drives 100 miles at 50 mph, stops for 30 minutes, then drives 150 miles at 60 mph. What is the average speed for the whole trip, including the stop?
questions.explain: Driving time is 100 / 50 = 2 hours plus 150 / 60 = 2.5 hours, and the stop adds 0.5 hour, for 5 hours. Average speed = 250 / 5 = 50 mph. Check: 50 x 5 = 250 miles. 55 averages the two speeds, about 55.6 leaves out the stop (250 / 4.5), 62.5 divides by only 4 hours, and about 41.7 divides by 6 hours.

questions.stem: An aircraft's maximum takeoff weight is 12,500 pounds. Its empty weight is 7,900 pounds, and crew plus cargo weigh 2,188 pounds. Fuel weighs 6.7 pounds per gallon. What is the greatest number of gallons of fuel it can carry?
questions.explain: Weight available for fuel = 12,500 - 7,900 - 2,188 = 2,412 pounds. At 6.7 pounds per gallon that is 2,412 / 6.7 = 360 gallons. Check: 360 x 6.7 = 2,160 + 252 = 2,412. 2,412 leaves the answer in pounds, 687 forgets the crew and cargo, 16,160 multiplies by 6.7 instead of dividing, and 402 uses 6 pounds per gallon.

questions.stem: Printer A prints 1,200 pages in 20 minutes, and printer B prints 1,200 pages in 30 minutes. Running together, how many minutes will they take to print 3,000 pages?
questions.explain: Printer A prints 1,200 / 20 = 60 pages per minute and printer B prints 1,200 / 30 = 40, so together they print 100 pages per minute. 3,000 / 100 = 30 minutes. Check: in 30 minutes A prints 1,800 and B prints 1,200, total 3,000. 50 uses printer A alone, 75 uses printer B alone, 62.5 scales the average time of 25 minutes per 1,200 pages, and 12 is the time for only 1,200 pages.

questions.stem: A supply bin holds 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green chemical light sticks. An airman takes two sticks at random without looking. What is the probability that both sticks are the same color?
questions.explain: There are 12 sticks, so the number of possible pairs is (12 x 11) / 2 = 66. Same-color pairs: red (5 x 4) / 2 = 10, blue (4 x 3) / 2 = 6, green (3 x 2) / 2 = 3, a total of 19. Probability = 19/66. 25/72 replaces the first stick before drawing the second, 5/33 (10/66) counts only red pairs, 1/3 assumes the three colors are equally likely, and 19/132 counts the favorable pairs once but the possible pairs in order.

questions.stem: Three radar sites work independently. The chances that each one detects a low-flying target are 80 percent, 70 percent and 50 percent. What is the probability that at least one site detects the target?
questions.explain: Work with the complement. The chance that every site misses is 0.20 x 0.30 x 0.50 = 0.03, so the chance that at least one detects it is 1 - 0.03 = 0.97, or 97 percent. 28 percent (0.8 x 0.7 x 0.5) is the chance that all three detect it, 3 percent is the chance that none does, 67 percent averages the three rates, and 22 percent is the chance that exactly one site detects it.

questions.stem: In a training game, two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the total is at least 10?
questions.explain: There are 6 x 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes. A total of 10 happens 3 ways (4-6, 5-5, 6-4), 11 happens 2 ways and 12 happens 1 way, so 6 outcomes work: 6/36 = 1/6. 1/12 counts only totals of 11 and 12, 3/11 treats the 11 possible totals as equally likely, 5/36 leaves out the 12, and 5/18 (10/36) counts totals of 9 or more.

questions.stem: A flight of 10 airmen has 6 men and 4 women. Two airmen are chosen at random for a detail. What is the probability that exactly one of the two is a woman?
questions.explain: The number of possible pairs is (10 x 9) / 2 = 45. Pairs with one woman and one man: 4 x 6 = 24. Probability = 24/45 = 8/15. Check by order: woman then man is 4/10 x 6/9 = 4/15, man then woman is also 4/15, total 8/15. 4/15 counts only one order, 2/5 is the chance a single pick is a woman, 12/25 picks with replacement (2 x 0.4 x 0.6), and 2/15 (6/45) is the chance both are women.

questions.stem: Crew A can overhaul an engine in 10 hours and crew B can do the same job in 15 hours. Both crews work together for 3 hours, then crew B is called away. How many more hours does crew A need to finish the job alone?
questions.explain: Together the crews do 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 1/6 of the job per hour, so in 3 hours they finish 3/6 = 1/2. Crew A does 1/10 per hour, so the remaining 1/2 takes (1/2) / (1/10) = 5 hours. Check: A's total of 8 hours gives 8/10, plus B's 3 hours gives 3/15 = 2/10, a whole job. 7.5 hours has crew B finish instead, 3 hours repeats the shared time, 8 hours is A's total time on the job, and 6 hours is how long the whole job would take together.

questions.stem: Working together, two technicians can calibrate a set of instruments in 4 hours. The faster technician alone takes 6 hours. How long would the slower technician take alone?
questions.explain: Rates add: the pair does 1/4 of the job per hour and the faster technician does 1/6, so the slower one does 1/4 - 1/6 = 3/12 - 2/12 = 1/12 per hour, which means 12 hours alone. Check: 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4. 2 hours subtracts the times (6 - 4), 10 hours adds them, 5 hours averages them, and 8 hours doubles the shared time.

questions.stem: How many liters of a 30 percent glycol solution must be mixed with 50 liters of an 80 percent glycol solution to produce a 50 percent solution?
questions.explain: Glycol before = glycol after: 0.30x + 0.80(50) = 0.50(x + 50), so 0.30x + 40 = 0.50x + 25, which gives 15 = 0.20x and x = 75 liters. Check: 22.5 + 40 = 62.5 liters of glycol in 125 liters is 50 percent. 50 liters assumes equal amounts, 33 1/3 liters flips the 3:2 ratio of the amounts, 125 liters is the total mixture, and 200 liters forgets to add the 50 liters to the final volume (0.30x + 40 = 0.50x).

questions.stem: A 200-pound batch of brine is 6 percent salt. How many pounds of water must be evaporated so that the brine is 10 percent salt?
questions.explain: Only water leaves, so the salt stays at 0.06 x 200 = 12 pounds. For 12 pounds to be 10 percent, the brine must weigh 12 / 0.10 = 120 pounds, so 200 - 120 = 80 pounds of water must evaporate. Check: 12 / 120 = 0.10. 120 pounds is the final weight, 8 pounds is the 4-point rise taken as a percent of 200, 133 1/3 pounds takes 4/6 of 200, and 48 pounds takes 40 percent of the final weight.

questions.stem: A squadron's monthly fuel use rose 60 percent during an exercise. By what percent must it now fall to return to its level before the exercise?
questions.explain: Call the original level 100. After a 60 percent rise it is 160. Falling back to 100 is a drop of 60 out of 160, and 60 / 160 = 0.375 = 37.5 percent. 60 percent forgets the drop is measured from the higher value, 40 percent is 100 - 60, 62.5 percent is the new level as a share of the old (100 / 160), and 30 percent halves the rise.

questions.stem: A unit's budget is 45 percent personnel costs and 55 percent operating costs. Next year personnel costs rise 20 percent and operating costs fall 10 percent. What is the overall change in the budget?
questions.explain: Use a budget of 100: personnel goes from 45 to 45 x 1.20 = 54, and operating goes from 55 to 55 x 0.90 = 49.5. The new total is 54 + 49.5 = 103.5, a 3.5 percent increase. 10 percent subtracts the two rates without weighting, 5 percent averages them, 6.5 percent swaps the weights (0.55 x 20 - 0.45 x 10), and 3.5 percent decrease has the right size but the wrong direction.

questions.stem: At a briefing the ratio of officers to enlisted members is 3:5. After 8 more officers arrive and no one leaves, the ratio becomes 1:1. How many people are at the briefing now?
questions.explain: Write the groups as 3k officers and 5k enlisted. After the arrivals 3k + 8 = 5k, so 2k = 8 and k = 4. That gives 12 + 8 = 20 officers and 20 enlisted, 40 people. Check: 12:20 = 3:5 before. 32 is the number before the arrivals, 20 counts only one group, 48 adds 8 to each group, and 24 is 3 x 8.

questions.stem: A forward base has enough fuel to support 8 aircraft for 15 days. After 3 days, 4 more aircraft arrive. Assuming every aircraft burns fuel at the same rate, for how many more days will the remaining fuel last?
questions.explain: The supply is 8 x 15 = 120 aircraft-days. After 3 days, 8 x 3 = 24 are used, leaving 96 aircraft-days. With 12 aircraft that lasts 96 / 12 = 8 days. 10 days scales the full 15 days by 8/12 and ignores the 3 days already used, 12 days ignores the new arrivals, 7 days scales the full 15 days first and then subtracts the 3 days used, and 18 days scales the wrong way (12 x 12/8).

questions.stem: A student's average on 8 quizzes is 84. If the lowest score is dropped, the average of the remaining 7 quizzes is 87. What was the lowest score?
questions.explain: Total of 8 scores = 8 x 84 = 672. Total of 7 scores = 7 x 87 = 609. The dropped score is 672 - 609 = 63. 81 subtracts the 3-point rise from 84, 60 takes 3 points x 8 quizzes away from 84, 78 subtracts twice the rise, and 66 subtracts 3 x 7 from 87.

questions.stem: Section A has 15 airmen with an average test score of 72. Section B's average is 84. The combined average of both sections is 80. How many airmen are in section B?
questions.explain: Set total points equal: 72(15) + 84b = 80(15 + b), so 1,080 + 84b = 1,200 + 80b, 4b = 120 and b = 30. Check: section A is 8 points below 80 and B is 4 above, so B needs twice as many airmen. 15 assumes equal sections, 7.5 flips the 2:1 ratio, 22.5 compares the whole 12-point spread with A's 8-point gap (15 x 12/8), and 45 is the combined total.

questions.stem: A training aircraft flies to a range at a ground speed of 300 knots and returns along the same route at 200 knots. The total flying time is 5 hours. How far is the range from base?
questions.explain: If d is the distance, d/300 + d/200 = 5. With 600 as the common denominator, 2d/600 + 3d/600 = 5d/600 = 5, so d = 600 nautical miles. Check: 2 hours out plus 3 hours back is 5 hours. 625 uses the average speed of 250 knots, 1,200 is the round-trip distance, and 500 and 750 split the 5 hours equally between the legs (2.5 hours at each speed).

questions.stem: If a convoy drives to a training area at 45 mph, it arrives 20 minutes late. If it drives at 60 mph, it arrives 10 minutes early. How far away is the training area?
questions.explain: The two trip times differ by 20 + 10 = 30 minutes, or 1/2 hour: d/45 - d/60 = 1/2. With 180 as the common denominator, 4d/180 - 3d/180 = d/180 = 1/2, so d = 90 miles. Check: 90/45 = 2 hours and 90/60 = 1.5 hours, a 30-minute difference. 30 miles uses a 10-minute gap (20 - 10), 60 miles uses only the 20 minutes, 45 miles assumes a one-hour trip, and 105 miles adds the two speeds.

questions.stem: An aircraft carries 9,000 pounds of usable fuel and burns 1,800 pounds per hour in transit at 300 knots. It must spend 1.5 hours on station, where it burns 1,200 pounds per hour, and must land with a 30-minute reserve at the transit burn rate. What is the farthest the station can be from base?
