questions.explain: Reserve = 0.5 x 1,800 = 900 pounds. On station = 1.5 x 1,200 = 1,800 pounds. That leaves 9,000 - 900 - 1,800 = 6,300 pounds for transit, or 6,300 / 1,800 = 3.5 hours out and back. One way is 1.75 hours x 300 = 525 nautical miles. 1,050 is the round-trip distance, 600 ignores the reserve, 675 ignores the fuel used on station, and 450 burns the on-station fuel at the transit rate.

questions.stem: A base exchange marks an item up 40 percent above its cost, then puts it on sale at 25 percent off the marked price. What is the profit or loss as a percent of cost?
questions.explain: Use a cost of $100. The marked price is $140, and 25 percent off leaves 0.75 x 140 = $105, a $5 profit on $100, or 5 percent. Check: 1.40 x 0.75 = 1.05. 15 percent subtracts the percents (40 - 25), 30 percent applies the discount only to the $40 markup, 5 percent loss gets the direction wrong, and about 4.8 percent measures the $5 profit against the $105 selling price instead of the cost.

questions.stem: On a 1:250,000 chart, two checkpoints are 7.2 centimeters apart. What is the actual distance between them?
questions.explain: Every centimeter on the chart is 250,000 centimeters on the ground: 7.2 x 250,000 = 1,800,000 centimeters. There are 100,000 centimeters in a kilometer, so the distance is 1,800,000 / 100,000 = 18 kilometers. 1.8 and 180 kilometers slip the decimal by one place, 72 kilometers treats each centimeter as 10 kilometers, and 1,800 kilometers converts with 1,000 centimeters per kilometer.

questions.stem: A pilot's first 5 sorties averaged 3.2 hours. What must the average length of the next 2 sorties be for the average of all 7 sorties to reach 3.6 hours?
questions.explain: The 7 sorties must total 7 x 3.6 = 25.2 hours. The first 5 total 5 x 3.2 = 16 hours, so the next 2 must total 25.2 - 16 = 9.2 hours, an average of 9.2 / 2 = 4.6 hours. 4.0 hours adds the 0.4 gap to 3.6, 9.2 hours is the total for both sorties, 2.8 hours uses 6 sorties instead of 7, and 5.6 hours is the 6-sortie shortfall without dividing by 2.

questions.stem: A student pilot has a 0.9 probability of passing each of three independent checkrides. What is the probability that the student passes exactly two of the three?
questions.explain: Passing two and failing one has probability 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.1 = 0.081 for each order, and the failed ride can be the first, second or third, so the total is 3 x 0.081 = 0.243. 0.081 counts only one order, 0.729 (0.9 cubed) is passing all three, 0.81 is passing two rides and ignores the third, and 0.27 multiplies 3 x 0.9 x 0.1 without squaring the 0.9.

questions.stem: Two aircraft are 900 nautical miles apart and fly directly toward each other, departing at the same time. One flies at 280 knots and the other at 320 knots. How far from the slower aircraft's starting point do they meet?
questions.explain: They close at 280 + 320 = 600 knots, so they meet after 900 / 600 = 1.5 hours. The slower aircraft has flown 280 x 1.5 = 420 nautical miles. Check: the faster one flew 320 x 1.5 = 480, and 420 + 480 = 900. 480 is the faster aircraft's distance, 450 assumes they meet halfway, 840 uses a 3-hour time from 900 / 300, and 525 multiplies 900 by 280/480 instead of 280/600.

questions.stem: Two warning beacons flash together at exactly 0800:00. One flashes every 12 seconds and the other every 18 seconds. How many more times do they flash together before 0810:00?
questions.explain: They flash together every LCM(12, 18) = 36 seconds. Ten minutes is 600 seconds, and 600 / 36 = 16.7, so they coincide 16 more times (the 16th at 576 seconds; the 17th would be at 612 seconds, after 0810:00). 17 rounds up or counts the 0800:00 flash, 50 counts the 12-second beacon's flashes, 33 counts the 18-second beacon's flashes, and 100 uses the GCF (6 seconds) instead of the LCM.

questions.stem: A courier charges $18.00 for the first 5 pounds of a package and $2.40 for each additional pound or part of a pound. What is the charge for a package weighing 12.3 pounds?
questions.explain: The package is 12.3 - 5 = 7.3 pounds over the first 5, and any part of a pound counts as a whole pound, so 8 additional pounds are charged: 8 x $2.40 = $19.20. Total = $18.00 + $19.20 = $37.20. $35.52 charges for exactly 7.3 pounds, $34.80 rounds down to 7 pounds, $47.52 charges $2.40 on all 12.3 pounds as well as the $18, and $29.52 charges only $2.40 per pound for the whole package.

questions.stem: Of 120 cadets, 70 are on the flying team, 46 are on the debate team, and 20 are on neither team. How many cadets are on both teams?
questions.explain: Cadets on at least one team = 120 - 20 = 100. Adding the team sizes counts the overlap twice: 70 + 46 = 116, so 116 - 100 = 16 are on both. 4 forgets the 20 cadets on neither team (116 - 120), 30 is the number on the debate team only, 54 is the number on the flying team only, and 20 is the number on neither.

questions.stem: A unit spends 1/4 of its budget on fuel and 2/5 of what remains on spare parts. It has $6,300 left. What was the original budget?
questions.explain: After fuel, 3/4 of the budget is left. Spare parts take 2/5 of that, leaving 3/5 of 3/4 = 9/20 of the budget. So 9/20 of the budget is $6,300, and the budget is 6,300 x 20/9 = $14,000. Check: fuel $3,500 leaves $10,500, parts take $4,200, leaving $6,300. $18,000 takes 2/5 of the whole budget (1 - 1/4 - 2/5 = 7/20), $8,400 undoes only the fuel step, $10,500 undoes only the parts step, and $25,200 treats $6,300 as the fuel share.

questions.stem: Machine A starts at 0700 and packs 120 boxes per hour. Machine B starts at 0900 and packs 180 boxes per hour. At what time will the two machines have packed a total of 1,440 boxes?
questions.explain: By 0900, machine A has packed 2 x 120 = 240 boxes, leaving 1,200. Together the machines pack 300 per hour, so the rest takes 1,200 / 300 = 4 hours, ending at 1300. Check: A runs 6 hours (720) and B runs 4 hours (720), total 1,440. 1148 runs both machines from 0700, 1348 ignores A's head start, 1100 counts the 4 hours from 0700, and 1540 has machine B finish the remaining 1,200 boxes alone.

questions.stem: A full rectangular tank 14 feet long, 5.5 feet wide and 3 feet deep is emptied into an empty cylindrical tank with a radius of 3.5 feet. How deep is the water in the cylinder? (Use pi = 22/7.)
questions.explain: The water's volume is 14 x 5.5 x 3 = 231 cubic feet. The cylinder's base area is pi r squared = (22/7) x 3.5 x 3.5 = 38.5 square feet, so the depth is 231 / 38.5 = 6 feet. 1.5 feet uses the 7-foot diameter as the radius, 10.5 feet divides by the circumference (22), 21 feet multiplies pi by the radius only once (11), and 3 feet assumes the depth stays the same.

questions.stem: A transport covers a route in 3 hours 20 minutes at 300 knots. How long would the same route take at 400 knots?
questions.explain: The distance is 300 x 3 1/3 = 1,000 nautical miles, and 1,000 / 400 = 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes. Equivalently, time varies inversely with speed: 200 minutes x 300/400 = 150 minutes. 4 hours 27 minutes multiplies by 400/300 instead, 2 hours 20 minutes subtracts an hour for the extra 100 knots, 2 hours 40 minutes takes 20 percent off the time, and 2 hours 50 minutes subtracts 30 minutes per 100 knots.

questions.stem: The average of five numbers is 18. The average of three of them is 15. What is the average of the other two?
questions.explain: The five numbers total 5 x 18 = 90 and the three total 3 x 15 = 45, so the other two total 90 - 45 = 45 and average 45 / 2 = 22.5. 21 adds the 3-point gap to 18, 33 adds the two averages, 45 is the total of the two numbers, and 16.5 averages the two given averages.

questions.stem: Aircraft X's range is 20 percent greater than aircraft Y's, and Y's range is 25 percent less than aircraft Z's. How does X's range compare with Z's?
questions.explain: Let Z's range be 100. Y's is 25 percent less, 75. X's is 20 percent more than 75: 75 x 1.20 = 90, which is 10 percent less than Z's. 5 percent less adds the percents (+20 - 25), equal assumes the changes cancel, 4 percent less treats Z as 25 percent more than Y (Y = 80, X = 96), and 10 percent more gets the direction wrong.

questions.stem: A contractor earns $32 per hour for the first 40 hours in a week and 1.5 times that rate for every hour beyond 40. One week she is paid $1,712. How many hours did she work?
questions.explain: The first 40 hours pay 40 x $32 = $1,280, leaving $1,712 - $1,280 = $432 of overtime. The overtime rate is 1.5 x $32 = $48, so she worked $432 / $48 = 9 overtime hours, 49 hours in all. 53.5 hours pays every hour at $32, 9 hours is the overtime only, 46.75 hours uses double time ($64 an hour), and 58 hours pays overtime at half the rate ($24).

questions.stem: Four crew members are assigned at random to four numbered seats, one per seat. What is the probability that the pilot gets seat 1 and the copilot gets seat 2?
questions.explain: The pilot lands in seat 1 with probability 1/4. Given that, the copilot lands in seat 2 with probability 1/3, since three seats remain. 1/4 x 1/3 = 1/12. Check: 2 of the 24 seatings (the other two crew in either order) work, and 2/24 = 1/12. 1/16 treats the two seats as independent (1/4 x 1/4), 1/4 covers only the pilot, 1/24 counts only one of the two seatings that work, and 7/12 adds 1/4 and 1/3 instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: A base air show sold 400 tickets. Adult tickets cost $12 and child tickets cost $7, and ticket sales totaled $4,050. How many child tickets were sold?
questions.explain: Let c be child tickets, so 400 - c are adult: 12(400 - c) + 7c = 4,050, which gives 4,800 - 5c = 4,050, so 5c = 750 and c = 150. Check: 250 x $12 = $3,000 and 150 x $7 = $1,050, total $4,050. 250 is the number of adult tickets, 200 splits the tickets evenly, 125 divides the $1,250 left after 400 x $7 by 10 instead of by the $5 price difference, and 107 divides the $750 shortfall by the $7 child price.

questions.stem: A helicopter flies 150 miles north, 50 miles east, 90 miles south and then 30 miles east. How far is it, in a straight line, from where it started?
questions.explain: Net north = 150 - 90 = 60 miles, and net east = 50 + 30 = 80 miles. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse: the square root of (60 squared + 80 squared) = the square root of 10,000 = 100 miles. 320 miles is the total path flown, 140 miles adds the two net legs, 170 miles ignores the southward leg (150 and 80), and 80 miles is the eastward component alone.

questions.stem: An aircraft at 33,000 feet must be level at 3,000 feet when it is 15 nautical miles from the airport. It descends at 2,000 feet per minute with a ground speed of 360 knots. How far from the airport must it begin its descent?
questions.explain: It must lose 33,000 - 3,000 = 30,000 feet, which takes 30,000 / 2,000 = 15 minutes. At 360 knots it covers 6 nautical miles a minute, so 15 x 6 = 90 nautical miles during the descent. Adding the 15 miles where it must already be level gives 105 nautical miles. 90 forgets the 15-mile point, 75 subtracts it, 99 descends all the way from 33,000 feet to the ground, and 114 adds 15 to that error.

questions.stem: An officer on temporary duty changes $1,500 into euros at 0.92 euros per dollar and spends 1,104 euros. She then changes the remaining euros back at 1.10 dollars per euro. How many dollars does she get back?
questions.explain: $1,500 x 0.92 = 1,380 euros. After spending 1,104 euros, 276 euros remain, and 276 x 1.10 = $303.60. $300.00 converts back with the first rate (276 / 0.92), $253.92 multiplies by 0.92 instead, $250.91 divides by 1.10 instead of multiplying, and $396.00 subtracts the 1,104 euros from the $1,500 as if they were dollars.

questions.stem: Six identical printers produce 4,800 pages in 40 minutes. At the same rate, how many pages can 9 of these printers produce in 25 minutes?
questions.explain: One printer makes 4,800 / (6 x 40) = 20 pages per minute. Nine printers for 25 minutes make 9 x 25 x 20 = 4,500 pages. Check: 4,800 x (9/6) x (25/40) = 4,500. 3,000 adjusts only for the time, 7,200 adjusts only for the printers, 11,520 inverts the time ratio, and 3,200 inverts the printer ratio.

questions.stem: An officer deposits $8,000 in an account paying 6 percent annual interest compounded semiannually. How much is in the account after one year?
questions.explain: Semiannual compounding pays 6 / 2 = 3 percent twice: 8,000 x 1.03 = 8,240 after six months, and 8,240 x 1.03 = 8,487.20 after a year. $8,480.00 is simple interest, $8,988.80 pays the full 6 percent each half-year, $8,240.00 stops after six months, and $487.20 is only the interest earned.

questions.stem: A dart lands at random on a square target 20 inches on a side. Painted on the target is a circle with a diameter of 10 inches. What is the probability that the dart lands inside the circle?
questions.explain: Probability = circle area / square area. The circle's radius is 5, so its area is 25 pi, and the square's area is 400. 25 pi / 400 = pi/16 (about 0.20). pi/4 would be a circle filling the square (diameter 20), 1/4 squares the ratio of the lengths and drops pi, pi/40 uses the circumference (10 pi) instead of the area, and 1/2 compares the diameter with the side.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PUSILLANIMOUS?
questions.explain: Pusillanimous means lacking courage or resolve; Latin pusillus (very small) plus animus (spirit), so a small-spirited person. Generous is the trap from its opposite magnanimous, undivided comes from unanimous, combative is a sound-alike slip toward pugnacious, and fussy confuses it with punctilious.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of OBSEQUIOUS?
questions.explain: Obsequious means excessively eager to please or obey, like a servile flatterer; think of someone who follows (Latin sequi) too closely. Obscure and obstinate only share the ob- opening, courteous is one shade off because plain politeness is not excessive or servile, and offensive is close to the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of LACONIC?
questions.explain: Laconic means using very few words; the Spartans of Laconia were famous for one-word replies. Lazy is a look-alike from lackadaisical, tearful comes from lachrymose, wordy is the opposite, and ironic only rhymes with it.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of RECALCITRANT?
questions.explain: Recalcitrant means stubbornly resisting authority or control; the Latin root pictures a mule kicking back with its heels (calx). Recurring and calculating are look-alikes, hesitant is a weaker near-miss because hesitating is not resisting, and repentant is roughly the opposite attitude.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PERFIDIOUS?
questions.explain: Perfidious means deliberately disloyal or treacherous; Latin per fidem, through or against faith, so faith broken. Flawless and perfumed play on the per- and perf- openings, persistent is a sound-alike, and loyal is the direct opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of TRUCULENT?
questions.explain: Truculent means eager to fight or argue, aggressively defiant; Latin trux means fierce. Candid is the trap from truthful, juicy comes from the rhyme succulent, fragile is unrelated, and meek is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of SYCOPHANT?
questions.explain: A sycophant is a self-serving flatterer who sucks up to powerful people. Psychic and skeptic are look-alike trap words, mentor is a related-sounding role but is a guide, not a toady, and critic is the opposite of a flatterer.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of INSOUCIANT?
questions.explain: Insouciant means casually unconcerned or carefree; French in- (not) plus soucier (to worry). Insolent and innocent share the in- opening, unsociable is a sound-alike, and anxious is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of EQUIVOCATE?
questions.explain: To equivocate is to use deliberately vague or double-meaning language to avoid committing yourself; equi (equal) plus voc (voice), speaking with two equal voices. Equalize grabs the equi- root, summon grabs the voc- (call) root, confess is the opposite of evading, and reconcile is unrelated.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of INTRANSIGENT?
questions.explain: Intransigent means refusing to change your position or compromise; in- (not) plus transigere (to come to terms). Temporary is the transient trap, transparent and migratory play on the trans- root, and conciliatory is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PERSPICACIOUS?
questions.explain: Perspicacious means having keen insight or judgment; per (through) plus specere (to look), seeing through things. Sweaty is the perspire trap, persistent is a sound-alike, lucid is the perspicuous trap (clearly expressed, said of writing, not of people's judgment), and suspicious only shares the -spic- letters.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of LOQUACIOUS?
questions.explain: Loquacious means very talkative; Latin loqui means to speak, as in eloquent and soliloquy. Eloquent is one shade off because it means expressive and persuasive, not talking a lot, reticent is the opposite, fluid is a sound-alike from liquid, and regional comes from the local look-alike.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of MENDACIOUS?
questions.explain: Mendacious means untruthful; Latin mendax means liar. Begging is the trap from mendicant, repairing comes from mend, malicious is a different vice that sounds similar, and candid is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of INEFFABLE?
questions.explain: Ineffable means too great or extreme to be put into words; in- (not) plus effari (to speak out). Ineffective and inedible are look-alikes, unerring is the trap from infallible, and unstoppable is unrelated.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PARSIMONIOUS?
questions.explain: Parsimonious means extremely unwilling to spend money, miserly; parsimony is excessive thrift. Generous is the opposite, cautious is a vague near-miss about risk rather than spending, pompous only shares the -ous ending and rhythm, and particular plays on the par- opening.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of ABSTRUSE?
questions.explain: Abstruse means difficult to understand, deep and obscure. Ridiculous comes from the look-alike absurd, dull-witted from obtuse, abrupt only shares ab-, and lucid is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of DIFFIDENT?
questions.explain: Diffident means modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence; dis- (not) plus fidere (to trust), not trusting yourself. Distinct comes from the look-alike different, defiant is a sound-alike, apathetic is the indifferent trap, and confident is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of FASTIDIOUS?
questions.explain: Fastidious means very attentive to accuracy and detail, hard to please; think of someone who fusses over every speck. Speedy is the fast trap, tedious and festive are sound-alikes, and slovenly is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of INCHOATE?
questions.explain: Inchoate means just begun and not yet fully formed; Latin inchoare means to begin. Inherent is a look-alike meaning built-in, finished is the opposite, dormant is one shade off because it means inactive rather than incomplete, and enclosed plays on the in- prefix.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PROPITIOUS?
questions.explain: Propitious means giving a good chance of success, favorable. Appeasing is the trap from the related verb propitiate, steep comes from the look-alike precipitous, unlucky is the opposite, and owned comes from proprietary.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of QUIXOTIC?
questions.explain: Quixotic means unrealistically idealistic and impractical, like Don Quixote tilting at windmills. Rapid is the quick trap, exotic shares the -otic sound, quizzical (puzzled or questioning) is a sound-alike, and pragmatic is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of SANGUINE?
questions.explain: Sanguine means cheerfully optimistic, from the old idea that a blood-rich temperament was hopeful. Sanitary is a look-alike about hygiene, gloomy is the opposite, saintly is a sound-alike from sanctity, and genuine only rhymes with it.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of TACITURN?
questions.explain: Taciturn means habitually saying very little; Latin tacere means to be silent. Tactful is a look-alike about diplomacy, implied is the trap from tacit (unspoken, said of an agreement, not a person), talkative is the opposite, and turbulent shares the -tur- sound.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of OBSTREPEROUS?
questions.explain: Obstreperous means noisy and difficult to control; Latin obstrepere means to make a noise against. Obsessive and obscure are ob- look-alikes, prosperous is a rhyme, and docile is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of EPHEMERAL?
questions.explain: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time; Greek ephemeros means lasting only a day. Delicate is the trap from the look-alike ethereal, everlasting is the opposite, imaginary confuses short-lived with unreal, and periodic means recurring, not brief.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of IMPECUNIOUS?
questions.explain: Impecunious means having little or no money; im- (not) plus pecunia (money), as in pecuniary. Flawless is the impeccable trap, odd comes from peculiar, wealthy is the opposite, and insolent comes from the look-alike impudent.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PULCHRITUDE?
questions.explain: Pulchritude is a formal word for physical beauty; Latin pulcher means beautiful. Decay is the putrefaction trap the ugly sound suggests, gratitude only rhymes, abundance comes from plenitude, and ugliness is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of RECONDITE?
questions.explain: Recondite means little known or understood by most people, obscure and specialized. Restored is the reconditioned trap, reconciled and conditional are look-alikes, and commonplace is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of APOCRYPHAL?
questions.explain: Apocryphal means of doubtful authenticity, widely told but probably untrue, like an apocryphal story about a famous pilot. Catastrophic is the apocalyptic trap, hypocritical is a sound-alike, cryptic is one shade off because it means mysterious rather than doubtful, and authentic is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of EXCULPATE?
questions.explain: To exculpate is to clear someone of blame; ex- (out of) plus culpa (guilt), as in culpable. Incriminate is the opposite, excavate and exaggerate are ex- look-alikes, and carve is the sculpt trap.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of VITUPERATIVE?
questions.explain: Vituperative means bitter and abusive in language, as in a vituperative tirade. Energetic is the vital trap, virtuous is a look-alike, flattering is the opposite, and vengeful is one shade off from vindictive because it is about revenge, not harsh words.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of MAGNANIMOUS?
questions.explain: Magnanimous means generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival; magnus (great) plus animus (spirit). Enormous seizes the magn- (big) root literally, undivided is the unanimous trap, petty is the opposite, and magnetic is a look-alike.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of SEDULOUS?
questions.explain: Sedulous means showing dedication and diligence, as in sedulous attention to the checklist. Seductive is a look-alike, inactive is the sedentary trap, calm is the sedate trap, and careless is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of TEMERITY?
questions.explain: Temerity means excessive confidence or boldness, nerve; Latin temere means rashly. Timidity is the classic look-alike and the opposite, moderation comes from temperance, persistence comes from tenacity, and brevity only rhymes.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of ALACRITY?
questions.explain: Alacrity means brisk and cheerful readiness, as in accepting a mission with alacrity. Bitterness is the acrimony trap, alarm shares the al- opening, reluctance is the opposite, and clarity only rhymes.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of CHICANERY?
questions.explain: Chicanery means the use of trickery and deception to achieve a goal, as in legal chicanery. Chivalry is a sound-alike, cowardice is the chicken trap, elegance is the chic trap, and candor is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of EXECRABLE?
questions.explain: Execrable means extremely bad or detestable; Latin exsecrari means to curse. Sacred is a root trap because the word is built on a curse, not a blessing, excusable is a look-alike, admirable is the opposite, and relentless is the inexorable trap.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PERFUNCTORY?
questions.explain: Perfunctory means done with minimum effort as a routine duty, as in a perfunctory preflight check. Thorough is the opposite, functional seizes the -funct- root, punctual is a sound-alike, and flawless plays on the perf- opening of perfect.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of INVETERATE?
questions.explain: Inveterate means having a long-established and unlikely-to-change habit, as in an inveterate gambler; Latin vetus means old. Spineless is the invertebrate trap, occasional is the opposite, inventive is a look-alike, and reversed comes from inverted.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of CONTUMACIOUS?
questions.explain: Contumacious means stubbornly disobedient to authority, a legal and military word for willfully defying orders. Infectious is the contagious trap, contemptible is a look-alike, compliant is the opposite, and quarrelsome is one shade off from contentious because it means argumentative, not defiant of authority.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of EXIGENT?
questions.explain: Exigent means pressing or demanding immediate action, as in exigent circumstances. Existent and exiled are look-alikes, meager is the trap from exiguous, and optional is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PROBITY?
questions.explain: Probity means strong moral principles, honesty and decency, a core expectation of officers. Likelihood is the probability trap, inquiry comes from probe, corruption is the opposite, and proximity only rhymes.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of EFFRONTERY?
questions.explain: Effrontery means insolent or shameless boldness, as in having the effrontery to question an order you ignored. Border is the frontier trap, effort is a look-alike, modesty is the opposite, and insult is one shade off from affront because it names an offense, not the brazen attitude.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of ABSTEMIOUS?
questions.explain: Abstemious means moderate and self-restrained, especially in eating and drinking; abs- (away from) plus temetum (strong drink). Gluttonous is the opposite, absent-minded and abrasive share the ab- opening, and sterile is a sound-alike from the -stem- letters.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of NEFARIOUS?
questions.explain: Nefarious means wicked or criminal; Latin nefas means a crime against divine law. Vague is the nebulous trap, nervous is a sound-alike, virtuous is the opposite, and varied confuses it with multifarious, which shares the -farious ending.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PROLIX?
questions.explain: Prolix means using too many words, tediously lengthy, as in a prolix briefing. Productive is the prolific trap, brief is the opposite, and proactive and prone (inclined to) are pro- look-alikes.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of OBVIATE?
questions.explain: To obviate is to remove a need or difficulty in advance, as in a backup system that obviates a manual reset. Clarify is the obvious trap, necessitate is the opposite, deviate shares the -viate ending, and obey shares the ob- opening.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of ESCHEW?
questions.explain: To eschew is to deliberately avoid or abstain from something, as in eschewing shortcuts. Chew is the visual trap inside the word, embrace is the opposite, and esteem and escort are es- look-alikes.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of VENAL?
questions.explain: Venal means open to bribery, willing to sell influence; Latin venum means sale. Pardonable is the venial trap (a venial sin is forgivable), springlike is the vernal trap, honest is the opposite, and venous is about veins.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of CAPRICIOUS?
questions.explain: Capricious means given to sudden, unaccountable changes of mood or behavior, like a goat (Italian capra) leaping unpredictably. Faultfinding is the captious trap, steadfast is the opposite, roomy is the capacious trap, and playful is a near-miss that lacks the changeable, unreliable sense.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of ENERVATE?
questions.explain: To enervate is to drain of energy or vitality; e- (out of) plus nervus (sinew), taking the sinews out. Energize is the classic opposite trap, revere is the venerate trap, enumerate is a look-alike, and embolden is the opposite in spirit.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of INIMICAL?
questions.explain: Inimical means tending to obstruct or harm, unfriendly; it shares the Latin inimicus (enemy) root with enemy. Unmatched is the inimitable trap, friendly is the opposite (amicable), comical is a rhyme, and minimal is a look-alike.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PALLIATE?
questions.explain: To palliate is to make a problem or pain less severe without removing its cause; Latin pallium means cloak, so you cloak the symptom. Whiten is the pale trap, aggravate is the opposite, befriend is the pal trap, and cure is one shade off because palliating eases without curing.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of LUGUBRIOUS?
questions.explain: Lugubrious means looking or sounding sad and dismal; Latin lugere means to mourn. Slippery is the lubricated trap, absurd is the ludicrous trap, cheerful is the opposite, and lavish is the luxurious trap.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of MALINGER?
questions.explain: To malinger is to pretend to be ill to avoid duty or work. Loiter is the linger trap hidden inside the word, slander is the malign trap, persevere is the opposite, and malfunction shares the mal- prefix but is about machines.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PEREMPTORY?
questions.explain: Peremptory means insisting on immediate attention or obedience, allowing no refusal, as in a peremptory order. Anticipatory is the preemptive trap, tentative is the opposite, temporary is a sound-alike, and permissive plays on the per- opening and is also the opposite in spirit.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of FECKLESS?
questions.explain: Feckless means lacking initiative or strength of character, useless and irresponsible; feck is an old Scots shortening of effect, so without effect. Flawless and fearless are -less look-alikes, capable is the opposite, and reckless is one shade off because it means heedless of danger, not ineffective.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of OBDURATE?
questions.explain: Obdurate means stubbornly unyielding and hardened against persuasion or feeling; Latin obdurare means to harden. Durable is the dur- (lasting) trap, obedient and obscure share only the ob- opening, and remorseful is the opposite of someone hardened in wrongdoing.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of TRENCHANT?
questions.explain: Trenchant means sharply perceptive and forceful, as in a trenchant critique; it comes from Old French trenchier, to cut. Deep-rooted confuses it with entrenched, defensive is the military trench trap, tedious misses the cutting sharpness, and vague is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PELLUCID?
questions.explain: Pellucid means transparent, letting light pass through clearly, and by extension very easy to understand, as in pellucid prose. Pale confuses it with pallid, fur-covered is the pelt trap, porous lets fluids through rather than light, and murky is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of SUPERCILIOUS?
questions.explain: Supercilious means behaving as if one is superior to others; Latin supercilium means eyebrow, from the raised brow of disdain. Shallow confuses it with superficial, excessive with superfluous, attentive with the sound-alike solicitous, and humble is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of IMPLACABLE?
questions.explain: Implacable means impossible to appease or pacify, as in an implacable enemy; Latin placare means to soothe. Calm confuses it with placid, misplaced is the place trap, flawless confuses it with impeccable, and forgiving is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of OBLOQUY?
questions.explain: Obloquy is strongly abusive or condemning speech, and also the disgrace that follows it; Latin obloqui means to speak against. Indirectness confuses it with oblique, monologue is the soliloquy trap from the shared -loquy ending, obligation shares only the obl- opening, and praise is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of DESULTORY?
questions.explain: Desultory means passing from one thing to another without plan or purpose, as in desultory conversation; a Latin desultor was a circus rider who leapt between horses. Humid is the sultry sound trap, abandoned confuses it with deserted, belittling confuses it with derogatory, and methodical is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PERNICIOUS?
questions.explain: Pernicious means highly harmful or destructive, often in a gradual way; Latin pernicies means destruction. Fussy confuses it with persnickety, treasured with precious, suspicious only shares the -icious ending, and beneficial is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of APLOMB?
questions.explain: Aplomb is self-assured composure, especially under strain, as in handling a crisis with aplomb; French à plomb meant upright like a plumb line. A lead weight is the plumb-bob trap from that origin, feathers confuses it with plumage, explosion is the bomb sound trap, and panic is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of MENDICANT?
questions.explain: A mendicant is a beggar, especially a member of a religious order that lives on alms; Latin mendicare means to beg. Liar confuses it with mendacious, repairer is the mend trap, merchant is a sound-alike, and donor is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PROPINQUITY?
questions.explain: Propinquity is nearness in place, time or relationship; Latin propinquus means near. Inclination confuses it with propensity, decency with propriety, ancientness only borrows the -quity ending of antiquity, and distance is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of QUERULOUS?
questions.explain: Querulous means habitually complaining in a peevish, whining way; Latin queri means to complain. Inquisitive is the query trap, chatty confuses it with garrulous, dangerous with perilous, and content is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PHLEGMATIC?
questions.explain: Phlegmatic means calm and unemotional, slow to be roused; it comes from phlegm, the bodily humor once blamed for a sluggish temperament. Practical confuses it with pragmatic, opinionated with dogmatic, sickly takes the phlegm root too literally, and excitable is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of LACHRYMOSE?
questions.explain: Lachrymose means tearful or given to weeping, as in a lachrymose farewell; Latin lacrima means tear. Glossy confuses it with lacquered, milky is the lact- (milk) trap, listless confuses it with lackadaisical, and cheerful is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of TORPID?
questions.explain: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, like an animal in hibernation; Latin torpere means to be numb. Scorching confuses it with torrid, lukewarm with tepid, murky with turbid, and energetic is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of PERIPATETIC?
questions.explain: Peripatetic means traveling from place to place, as in a peripatetic military family; Greek peripatein means to walk about. Marginal confuses it with peripheral, pitiable with pathetic, visionary with prophetic, and sedentary is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of MERETRICIOUS?
questions.explain: Meretricious means attractive in a showy, cheap or insincere way, as in meretricious decor or a meretricious argument. Praiseworthy is the classic trap from meritorious, greedy confuses it with mercenary, painstaking with meticulous, and understated is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the synonym of SALUBRIOUS?
questions.explain: Salubrious means favorable to health, as in a salubrious mountain climate; Latin salus means health. Salty is the sal- (salt) trap, mournful confuses it with lugubrious, slippery with lubricious, and unwholesome is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of MUNIFICENT?
questions.explain: Munificent means extremely generous, as in a munificent donation; Latin munus (gift) plus facere (make). Its antonym is stingy. Lavish is the synonym trap, civic is the meaning of the look-alike municipal, splendid comes from magnificent, and wealthy is a different money word, since a rich person need not give and a poor one can.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of VOLUBLE?
questions.explain: Voluble means speaking fluently, readily and at length; Latin volvere, to roll, as words roll off the tongue. Its antonym is reticent, reluctant to speak. Talkative is the synonym trap, bulky comes from voluminous, explosive from volatile, and dissolvable from soluble, which only rhymes.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of BELLICOSE?
questions.explain: Bellicose means eager to fight or go to war; Latin bellum, war, as in belligerent. Its antonym is peaceable. Combative is the synonym trap, bellowing is a sound-alike, beautiful is the bella (lovely) trap and bloated is the belly trap.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of DUPLICITOUS?
questions.explain: Duplicitous means deceitful through double-dealing, saying one thing and doing another. Its antonym is forthright, direct and honest. Deceitful is the synonym trap; copied (duplicated) and twofold (duplex) share the dupl- root but mean double, not dishonest, and convoluted only shares the complicated feel.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of DOLOROUS?
questions.explain: Dolorous means full of sorrow or grief; Latin dolor, pain, as in the dolorous tolling of a bell. Its antonym is joyful. Mournful is the synonym trap, smelly is the meaning of the rhyme odorous, costly is a dollar sound-alike, and languid (listless) is a different low-energy word, not the opposite of sorrow.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of PROFLIGATE?
questions.explain: Profligate means recklessly extravagant with money or resources, as in profligate spending. Its antonym is thrifty. Wasteful is the synonym trap, and profitable, productive (prolific) and skilled (proficient) are pro- look-alikes with unrelated meanings.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of EXPEDITIOUS?
questions.explain: Expeditious means done with speed and efficiency, as in an expeditious response; Latin expedire, to free the feet. Its antonym is sluggish. Speedy is the synonym trap, exploratory is the expedition trap, advantageous is the meaning of expedient, which shares the root but not the sense of speed, and ambitious only rhymes.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of INTRACTABLE?
questions.explain: Intractable means hard to control or deal with, as in an intractable problem or an intractable child; in- (not) plus tractare (handle). Its antonym is docile, easily managed. Unruly is the synonym trap, untouchable is the meaning of intangible, and attractive and distracted share the tract root but mean something else.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of POLTROON?
questions.explain: A poltroon is an utter coward. Its antonym is hero. Coward is the synonym trap, sponsor is the meaning of the look-alike patron, squad comes from platoon and clown from the rhyme buffoon.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of ACRIMONIOUS?
questions.explain: Acrimonious means angry and bitter, as in an acrimonious divorce; Latin acer, sharp. Its antonym is cordial, warm and friendly. Rancorous is the synonym trap, pungent is the meaning of acrid, which shares the sharp root but describes smell, formal comes from the rhyme ceremonious and marital from matrimonial.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of SANCTIMONIOUS?
questions.explain: Sanctimonious means making a show of being morally better than others. Its antonym is humble. Self-righteous is the synonym trap, sacred shares the sanct (holy) root but describes something truly holy, approved is the meaning of sanctioned and stingy comes from the rhyme parsimonious.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of REFRACTORY?
questions.explain: Refractory means stubbornly resistant to authority or control; Latin refringere, to break up. Its antonym is compliant. Unmanageable is the synonym trap, light-bending is the meaning of refractive, which shares the root, partial comes from fractional and refreshing is a re- look-alike.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of SOPORIFIC?
questions.explain: Soporific means tending to cause sleep, as in a soporific lecture; Latin sopor, deep sleep. Its antonym is stimulating. Sleep-inducing is the synonym trap, sophisticated shares only the opening letters, high-pitched comes from soprano and irregular from sporadic.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of VERACITY?
questions.explain: Veracity means truthfulness or accuracy; Latin verus, true. Its antonym is dishonesty. Truthfulness is the synonym trap, and greed (voracity), speed (velocity) and liveliness (vivacity) are the meanings of one-letter look-alikes.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of AGGRANDIZE?
questions.explain: To aggrandize is to increase the power, rank or importance of someone or something, as in a self-aggrandizing speech. Its antonym is diminish. Exalt is the synonym trap; aggravate (make worse), aggregate (collect) and agonize (worry) are ag- look-alikes with unrelated meanings.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of DEMUR?
questions.explain: To demur is to raise doubts or objections, as in 'she demurred at the cost'. Its antonym is consent. Object is the synonym trap, act shy is the trap from the look-alike adjective demure (modest), mutter comes from the rhyme murmur and demote only shares the de- opening.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of QUIESCENT?
questions.explain: Quiescent means in a state of inactivity or rest, as in a quiescent volcano; Latin quiescere, to rest. Its antonym is active. Dormant is the synonym trap, compliant is the meaning of acquiescent, which shares the root but means giving in, puzzled comes from quizzical and typical from quintessential.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of ESOTERIC?
questions.explain: Esoteric means understood by only a small, specialized group, as in esoteric jargon. Its antonym is mainstream, familiar to most people. Arcane is the synonym trap, foreign is the meaning of the look-alike exotic, artistic comes from aesthetic, and eccentric (odd) is a different idea, not the other end of the scale.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of OBTUSE?
questions.explain: Obtuse means slow to understand or notice, as in 'don't be obtuse'. Its antonym is perceptive. Dull-witted is the synonym trap, overweight is the obese look-alike, hard to understand is the meaning of abstruse, which describes an idea rather than a person, and intrusive comes from obtrusive.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of FRACTIOUS?
questions.explain: Fractious means irritable and hard to control, as in a fractious crowd. Its antonym is agreeable. Irritable is the synonym trap, broken is the fractured trap from the shared fract root, accurate is the meaning of the look-alike factual and fictitious only shares the -itious ending.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of EBULLIENT?
questions.explain: Ebullient means cheerful and bursting with energy; Latin ebullire, to boil over. Its antonym is subdued. Exuberant is the synonym trap, boiling is the literal root meaning rather than the sense of the word, obedient is a sound-alike and wealthy comes from affluent.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of VENERATE?
questions.explain: To venerate is to regard with deep respect, as people venerate a war hero. Its antonym is scorn. Revere is the synonym trap, produce is the meaning of the rhyme generate, air out comes from ventilate and weaken from the look-alike enervate.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of CONCILIATORY?
questions.explain: Conciliatory means intended to calm anger and win goodwill, as in a conciliatory gesture. Its antonym is antagonistic. Appeasing is the synonym trap, advisory is a trap from council, and concise and conspiratorial only share the con- opening.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of RAPACIOUS?
questions.explain: Rapacious means aggressively greedy, grasping for wealth or prey; Latin rapere, to seize. Its antonym is generous. Grasping is the synonym trap, swift is the rapid trap, roomy is the meaning of the rhyme capacious and ecstatic comes from rapturous.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of IGNOMINIOUS?
questions.explain: Ignominious means deserving or causing public disgrace, as in an ignominious defeat; in- (not) plus nomen (name), so losing one's good name. Its antonym is honorable. Disgraceful is the synonym trap, nameless takes the root too literally, uninformed comes from ignorant and threatening from the rhyme ominous.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of AFFABLE?
questions.explain: Affable means friendly and easy to talk to. Its antonym is surly, rude and bad-tempered. Amiable is the synonym trap, affordable is a look-alike, legendary comes from fable and expressible is the meaning of effable, a one-letter twin.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of EFFUSIVE?
questions.explain: Effusive means expressing feelings in a gushing, unrestrained way, as in effusive thanks; ex- (out) plus fundere (pour). Its antonym is reserved. Gushing is the synonym trap, spread out is the meaning of diffuse, which shares the root, and efficient and elusive (hard to catch) are look-alikes.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of GREGARIOUS?
questions.explain: Gregarious means fond of company, or living in flocks; Latin grex, flock. Its antonym is solitary. Sociable is the synonym trap, flagrant is the meaning of egregious, which shares the greg root, huge comes from gargantuan and serious from the sound-alike grievous.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of DISPARAGE?
questions.explain: To disparage is to speak of something as having little worth, as in disparaging remarks. Its antonym is praise. Belittle is the synonym trap, despair and scatter (disperse) are dis- look-alikes, and compare shares the par (equal) root but is neutral, not the opposite of belittling.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of INSIPID?
questions.explain: Insipid means lacking flavor or interest, as in insipid food or an insipid film; in- (not) plus sapidus (tasty). Its antonym is flavorful. Bland is the synonym trap, beginning is the meaning of the sound-alike incipient, sneaky comes from insidious and timid only rhymes.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of PROSAIC?
questions.explain: Prosaic means dull and lacking imagination, as in a prosaic explanation. Its antonym is imaginative. Mundane is the synonym trap, unrhymed takes the prose root too literally, tiled comes from the rhyme mosaic and prosperous only shares the pros- opening.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of AUDACIOUS?
questions.explain: Audacious means boldly daring, sometimes recklessly so; Latin audax, bold. Its antonym is timid. Daring is the synonym trap, hearable is the meaning of the look-alike audible, greedy comes from avaricious and dreadful from atrocious.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of OPAQUE?
questions.explain: Opaque means not letting light through, or hard to understand, as in opaque instructions. Its antonym is transparent. Murky is the synonym trap, luxurious is the meaning of opulent, slanting comes from oblique and optical only shares the op- opening.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of CORPULENT?
questions.explain: Corpulent means fat, having a large, bulky body; Latin corpus, body. Its antonym is gaunt, lean and haggard. Obese is the synonym trap, bodily is the meaning of corporal, which shares the root, dishonest comes from corrupt and juicy from the rhyme succulent.

questions.stem: What is the antonym of INNOCUOUS?
questions.explain: Innocuous means not harmful or offensive, as in an innocuous remark; in- (not) plus nocere (harm). Its antonym is injurious, causing harm. Harmless is the synonym trap, guiltless is the meaning of innocent, which shares the root, vaccinated comes from inoculated and nightly from nocturnal.

questions.stem: 3/8 + 5/12 − 1/6 is equal to
questions.explain: The least common denominator is 24: 3/8 = 9/24, 5/12 = 10/24 and 1/6 = 4/24. Then 9/24 + 10/24 − 4/24 = 15/24, which reduces to 5/8. 1/2 comes from combining numerators and denominators straight across, 23/24 adds the 1/6, 19/24 drops the last term, and 13/24 miswrites 5/12 as 8/24.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the greatest value?
questions.explain: Convert each to a decimal: 7/11 = 0.6363..., 5/8 = 0.625, 0.62, 61.5% = 0.615 and 0.6. The largest is 7/11. 5/8 is the most common pick because it looks largest, but 0.625 is less than 0.636; the others are smaller still.

questions.stem: For nonzero x and y, (x²y⁻³)⁻² ÷ (x⁻¹y)³ simplifies to
questions.explain: First (x²y⁻³)⁻² = x⁻⁴y⁶ and (x⁻¹y)³ = x⁻³y³. Dividing subtracts exponents: x^(−4 − (−3)) y^(6 − 3) = x⁻¹y³ = y³/x. xy³ is a sign slip on the x exponent, y⁹/x⁷ adds the exponents instead of subtracting, y³/x⁷ subtracts correctly for y but adds for x, and x/y³ is the reciprocal.

A negative exponent means take the reciprocal, so (16/81)^(−3/4) = (81/16)^(3/4). The fourth root of 81/16 is 3/2, and cubing gives 27/8. 8/27 forgets the reciprocal, −27/8 treats the negative exponent as a negative sign, 3/2 takes the fourth root but forgets to cube, and 729/64 takes the square root instead of the fourth root before cubing.
27^(4/3) = (∛27)⁴ = 3⁴ = 81, and 9^(−1/2) = 1/√9 = 1/3. So the product is 81 × 1/3 = 27. 81 ignores the second factor, 243 treats 9^(−1/2) as 3, −27 treats it as −1/3, and −243 treats it as −3.

questions.stem: √50 + √18 − √8 is equal to
questions.explain: Simplify each radical: √50 = 5√2, √18 = 3√2 and √8 = 2√2. Then 5√2 + 3√2 − 2√2 = 6√2. √60 wrongly combines the numbers under the radical signs, 10√2 adds the √8, 8√2 drops it, and 4√2 reverses the signs of the last two terms.

questions.stem: 6/(3 − √3) is equal to
questions.explain: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 3 + √3: the denominator becomes 9 − 3 = 6, and the numerator 6(3 + √3). Dividing by 6 gives 3 + √3. 3 − √3 uses the wrong sign, (3 + √3)/2 gets the denominator as 9 + 3 = 12, −3 − √3 computes it as 3 − 9, and 18 + 6√3 never divides by 6.

Work with the numbers and the powers separately: 6.0 × 5.0 ÷ 1.5 = 20, and 10^(−4 + 7 − 2) = 10¹. So the result is 20 × 10¹ = 200 = 2.0 × 10². 2.0 × 10¹ forgets to adjust the exponent when 20 becomes 2.0, 4.5 × 10² multiplies by 1.5 instead of dividing, 2.0 × 10⁶ adds the 10² instead of subtracting it, and 2.0 × 10⁻⁸ subtracts the 7.

questions.stem: 18 − 12 ÷ 3 × 2 + 2³ is equal to
questions.explain: Exponents first: 2³ = 8. Then multiply and divide left to right: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, then 4 × 2 = 8. Finally 18 − 8 + 8 = 18. 24 divides 12 by (3 × 2), 12 subtracts before dividing, 16 treats 2³ as 6, and 2 subtracts 8 + 8 together.

questions.stem: −3² + (−2)³ − 4(−1)⁵ is equal to
questions.explain: −3² means −(3²) = −9, (−2)³ = −8, and −4(−1)⁵ = −4(−1) = +4. So −9 − 8 + 4 = −13. 5 treats −3² as +9, −21 treats −4(−1)⁵ as −4, 3 treats (−2)³ as +8, and 21 makes every term positive.

questions.stem: 12x³y² − 18x²y³ + 6x²y², factored completely, is
questions.explain: The greatest common factor is 6x²y² (largest number dividing 12, 18 and 6, lowest powers of x and y). Dividing each term by it leaves 2x, −3y and 1. Dropping the 1 is the classic error (6x²y² ÷ 6x²y² = 1, not 0); the other choices swap the coefficients, lose the minus sign, or divide the terms incorrectly.

questions.stem: The complete factorization of 18x² − 50 is
questions.explain: Take out the common factor 2: 18x² − 50 = 2(9x² − 25). Then 9x² − 25 is a difference of squares, (3x − 5)(3x + 5). 2(3x − 5)² gives a middle term, (3x − 5)(3x + 5) forgets the 2, and (9x − 10)(2x + 5) and 2(9x − 5)(x + 5) match the end terms but produce an x term when multiplied out.

questions.stem: 6x² − 7x − 20 factors as
questions.explain: Check the middle term: (3x + 4)(2x − 5) = 6x² − 15x + 8x − 20 = 6x² − 7x − 20. (3x − 4)(2x + 5) gives +7x (signs reversed), (6x + 5)(x − 4) gives −19x, (2x + 4)(3x − 5) gives +2x, and (3x + 5)(2x − 4) gives −2x. Every choice has the right first and last terms, so only the middle term decides it.

questions.stem: For all values where it is defined, (x² − 9)/(x² + x − 6) simplifies to
questions.explain: Factor both parts: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and x² + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2). Cancel the common factor (x + 3) to get (x − 3)/(x − 2). (x + 3)/(x − 2) cancels the wrong factor, (x − 3)/(x + 2) factors the denominator with the wrong signs, and −9/(x − 6) and 3/2 cancel terms instead of factors.

questions.stem: For all values where it is defined, [(x² − 4x)/(x² − 16)] ÷ [2x/(x + 4)] simplifies to
questions.explain: Dividing means multiplying by the reciprocal: [x(x − 4)/((x − 4)(x + 4))] × [(x + 4)/(2x)]. The x, the (x − 4) and the (x + 4) all cancel, leaving 1/2. 2 flips the wrong fraction, 2x²/(x + 4)² multiplies without flipping, and x/2 and (x − 4)/2 leave behind a factor that actually cancels.

questions.stem: For nonzero x and y with x ≠ −y, (1/x − 1/y) ÷ (1/x + 1/y) is equal to
questions.explain: Multiply the top and bottom of the complex fraction by xy: the top becomes y − x and the bottom becomes y + x, giving (y − x)/(y + x). (x − y)/(x + y) gets the subtraction backwards, −1 cancels the 1/x terms as if they were factors, (y − x)/(xy) simplifies only the numerator, and (x + y)/(y − x) is the reciprocal.

Multiply every term by 12: 3(2x − 3) − 4(x + 1) = 12, so 6x − 9 − 4x − 4 = 12. Then 2x − 13 = 12, 2x = 25 and x = 25/2. 17/2 distributes −4 as −4x + 4, 7 forgets to multiply the right side by 12, 13/2 drops the right side, and 1/2 moves 13 with the wrong sign.

questions.stem: Solving A = P(1 + rt) for t gives t =
questions.explain: Distribute: A = P + Prt. Subtract P: A − P = Prt. Divide by Pr: t = (A − P)/(Pr). (A − 1)/(Pr) divides by P before subtracting and loses track of it, A/(Pr) − 1 subtracts 1 instead of 1/r, (A − P)/r forgets to divide by P, and Pr/(A − P) is upside down.

questions.stem: The solution of −3(x − 2) ≥ 2x + 21 is
questions.explain: Distribute: −3x + 6 ≥ 2x + 21. Subtract 2x and 6: −5x ≥ 15. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality, so x ≤ −3. x ≥ −3 forgets to reverse the sign, x ≤ 3 and x ≥ 3 slip the sign of the answer, and x ≤ −27/5 distributes −3(−2) as −6.

questions.stem: The solution of −7 < 3 − 2x ≤ 9 is
questions.explain: Subtract 3 from all three parts: −10 < −2x ≤ 6. Divide by −2 and reverse both signs: 5 > x ≥ −3, which reads −3 ≤ x < 5. −3 < x ≤ 5 reverses the signs but puts the 'or equal to' on the wrong end, −5 < x ≤ 3 and −5 ≤ x < 3 lose the negative when dividing, and the 'or' answer describes the values outside the interval.

questions.stem: The solutions of 2x² + 5x − 12 = 0 are
questions.explain: Factor: 2x² + 5x − 12 = (2x − 3)(x + 4), since 8x − 3x = 5x. Set each factor to zero: 2x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3/2 and x + 4 = 0 gives x = −4. −3/2 and 4 reverse both signs, 3 forgets to divide by 2, 2/3 divides the wrong way, and 3/2 with 4 slips one sign.

questions.stem: The solutions of x² − 4x − 1 = 0 are
questions.explain: Use x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/2a with a = 1, b = −4, c = −1: x = (4 ± √(16 + 4))/2 = (4 ± 2√5)/2 = 2 ± √5. −2 ± √5 uses b instead of −b, 2 ± √3 computes the discriminant as 16 − 4, 4 ± 2√5 forgets to divide by 2a, and 2 ± 2√5 divides only the first term by 2.

questions.stem: 2x² + kx + 8 = 0 has no real solutions exactly when
questions.explain: There are no real solutions when the discriminant is negative: k² − 4(2)(8) < 0, so k² < 64 and −8 < k < 8. k < −8 or k > 8 is the condition for two real solutions, −4√2 < k < 4√2 drops the a = 2 (using k² < 32), −4 < k < 4 halves the bound, and k < 8 forgets the lower bound, so it wrongly includes values such as k = −10.

questions.stem: If r and s are the roots of 3x² − 12x + 7 = 0, then r² + s² =
questions.explain: Without solving for the roots, use r + s = −b/a = 4 and rs = c/a = 7/3. Then r² + s² = (r + s)² − 2rs = 16 − 14/3 = 34/3. 16 stops at (r + s)², 41/3 subtracts rs instead of 2rs, 62/3 adds 2rs instead of subtracting it, and 2 uses rs = 7 by forgetting to divide c by a.

questions.stem: If 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x − 3y = 14, then the simultaneous solution is
questions.explain: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 2: 9x + 6y = 48 and 10x − 6y = 28. Adding gives 19x = 76, so x = 4, and then 12 + 2y = 16 gives y = 2. x = 2, y = 5 and x = 6, y = −1 satisfy only the first equation, x = 1, y = −3 satisfies only the second, and x = −4, y = −2 satisfies neither.

questions.stem: If x + y = 7 and x² − y² = 21, then x =
questions.explain: Factor x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y). Since x + y = 7, 7(x − y) = 21, so x − y = 3. Adding x + y = 7 and x − y = 3 gives 2x = 10, so x = 5 (and y = 2). 2 is y, 3 is x − y, 7 is x + y, and 10 is 2x or the product xy.

questions.stem: The solutions of |2x − 5| = 9 are
questions.explain: An absolute value equation splits into two cases: 2x − 5 = 9 gives x = 7, and 2x − 5 = −9 gives 2x = −4, x = −2. 'x = 7 only' misses the negative case, x = 2 drops the minus sign in the second case, and the other choices reverse signs.

questions.stem: The solution of |3x + 1| < 8 is
questions.explain: |3x + 1| < 8 means −8 < 3x + 1 < 8. Subtract 1: −9 < 3x < 7. Divide by 3: −3 < x < 7/3. x < 7/3 ignores the lower bound, the 'or' answer is the solution of |3x + 1| > 8, −7/3 < x < 3 subtracts 1 with the wrong sign, and −3 < x < 3 assumes the interval is symmetric.

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2x − 3 and g(x) = x² + 1, what positive value of x makes f(g(x)) = 17?
questions.explain: Substitute g into f: f(g(x)) = 2(x² + 1) − 3 = 2x² − 1. Setting 2x² − 1 = 17 gives x² = 9, so the positive value is x = 3. 7/2 solves g(f(x)) = 17, composing in the wrong order; 10 is the value of g(x), not x; 9 stops at x²; and 2√2 comes from simplifying f(g(x)) to 2x² + 1 instead of 2x² − 1.

questions.stem: If f(x) = (3x − 2)/5, then the inverse function f⁻¹(x) =
questions.explain: Write y = (3x − 2)/5, swap x and y, and solve: x = (3y − 2)/5, so 5x = 3y − 2, 3y = 5x + 2 and y = (5x + 2)/3. (5x − 2)/3 keeps the −2 instead of undoing it, 5/(3x − 2) is the reciprocal, not the inverse, (3x + 2)/5 only changes a sign, and 5x/3 + 2 adds 2 after dividing instead of before.

questions.stem: The line through (−3, 4) and (5, −2) has the equation
questions.explain: Slope = (−2 − 4)/(5 − (−3)) = −6/8 = −3/4. Substitute (−3, 4): 4 = −(3/4)(−3) + b = 9/4 + b, so b = 7/4. 25/4 adds 9/4 instead of subtracting it, (3/4)x + 25/4 and −(4/3)x both pass through (−3, 4) but have the wrong slope (sign error, rise and run swapped), and −2 uses a y-coordinate as the intercept.

questions.stem: The line perpendicular to 4x − 6y = 12 that passes through (2, 1) is
questions.explain: Rewrite 4x − 6y = 12 as y = (2/3)x − 2, so its slope is 2/3 and a perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal, −3/2. Then 1 = −(3/2)(2) + b = −3 + b, so b = 4. (2/3)x − 1/3 is the parallel line, −(3/2)x − 2 subtracts 3 instead of adding it, (3/2)x − 2 takes the reciprocal without changing the sign, and −(2/3)x + 7/3 changes the sign without taking the reciprocal.

questions.stem: The distance between the points (−2, 3) and (4, −5) is
questions.explain: d = √((4 − (−2))² + (−5 − 3)²) = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10. 14 adds the horizontal and vertical distances instead of using the Pythagorean theorem, 2√2 adds the coordinates instead of subtracting them, 100 forgets the square root, and 8 is only the vertical change.

questions.stem: M(2, 1) is the midpoint of segment AB. If A is (−3, 7), then B is
questions.explain: The midpoint is the average of the endpoints, so each coordinate of B is 2 × M − A: x = 2(2) − (−3) = 7 and y = 2(1) − 7 = −5. (−1/2, 4) is the midpoint of A and M, (5, −6) is only the change from A to M, (−8, 13) goes the same distance in the wrong direction, and (7, 9) adds 7 instead of subtracting it in the y-coordinate.

questions.stem: The complement of an angle is one-fourth of its supplement. The angle measures
questions.explain: Let the angle be x: 90 − x = (1/4)(180 − x). Multiply by 4: 360 − 4x = 180 − x, so 180 = 3x and x = 60°. Check: the complement is 30° and the supplement is 120°, and 30 is one-fourth of 120. 30° and 120° are the complement and supplement themselves, and 45° and 36° fail the check (45 is not a quarter of 135, and 54 is not a quarter of 144).

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate interior angles measure (3x + 10)° and (5x − 30)°. The measure of each angle is
questions.explain: Alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines are equal: 3x + 10 = 5x − 30, so 40 = 2x and x = 20. Each angle is 3(20) + 10 = 70°. 20° is x, not the angle; 110° is the supplement; and 25° and 85° come from wrongly treating the angles as supplementary (8x − 20 = 180).

questions.stem: An exterior angle of a triangle measures 130°. The two remote interior angles measure (2x)° and (3x + 5)°. The largest interior angle of the triangle measures
questions.explain: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 2x + 3x + 5 = 130, so x = 25 and the angles are 50° and 80°. The third interior angle is 180 − 130 = 50°, so the largest is 80°. 130° is the exterior angle, 50° is the smaller angle, 25° is x, and 75° forgets the +5.

questions.stem: Which of the following could be the side lengths of a triangle?
questions.explain: Any two sides of a triangle must add to more than the third side. For 4, 9, 12: 4 + 9 = 13 > 12, so it works. For 3, 5, 8 the two short sides only equal the third (a flat line), and 2 + 7 = 9, 5 + 5 = 10 and 6 + 7 = 13 are all less than the longest side.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a diagonal of 17 inches and a length of 15 inches. Its area, in square inches, is
questions.explain: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle: width² = 17² − 15² = 289 − 225 = 64, so the width is 8. Area = 15 × 8 = 120. 255 multiplies the length by the diagonal, 46 is the perimeter, 60 is the area of the triangle (half the rectangle), and 136 multiplies the width by the diagonal.

questions.stem: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, the side opposite the 60° angle is 9. The hypotenuse is
questions.explain: The sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. The side opposite 60° is the √3 side, so the short leg is 9/√3 = 3√3 and the hypotenuse is twice that, 6√3. 18 treats 9 as the short leg, 3√3 is the short leg itself, 9√2 uses the 45°-45°-90° ratio, and 9√3 multiplies by √3 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, with AB corresponding to DE. If AB = 6, DE = 9 and the area of triangle ABC is 24, the area of triangle DEF is
questions.explain: The scale factor is 9/6 = 3/2. Areas scale by the square of that factor: 24 × (3/2)² = 24 × 9/4 = 54. 36 scales the area by the linear factor 3/2, 16 uses the factor upside down, 81 squares DE, and 72 multiplies the area by 3.

questions.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures 156°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explain: Each exterior angle is 180 − 156 = 24°, and the exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 24 = 15. Check: (15 − 2) × 180 ÷ 15 = 156. 13 and 17 subtract or add the 2 from the angle-sum formula, 24 is the exterior angle itself, and 10 is a guess from 360 ÷ 36.

questions.stem: How many diagonals does a decagon (10-sided polygon) have?
questions.explain: Each vertex connects by a diagonal to n − 3 other vertices (not itself or its two neighbors), and each diagonal is counted twice, so the number is n(n − 3)/2 = 10 × 7 ÷ 2 = 35. 70 forgets to divide by 2, 45 counts every pair of vertices including the 10 sides, 7 is the diagonals from one vertex, and 20 is 10 × 2.

questions.stem: In a circle of radius 9, an inscribed angle measures 40°. The length of the arc it intercepts is
questions.explain: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc, so the arc measures 80°. Arc length = (80/360) × 2π(9) = (2/9) × 18π = 4π. 2π uses 40° as the arc, 8π doubles the arc twice, 18π is the sector area (80/360 × 81π) or the whole circumference, and 9π is half the circumference.

questions.stem: A right circular cylinder has radius 3 and height 8. Its total surface area is
questions.explain: Total surface area = two circular bases + the curved side = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2π(9) + 2π(3)(8) = 18π + 48π = 66π. 72π is the volume (πr²h), 48π is the curved side only, 57π counts only one base, and 96π uses the diameter in place of the radius for the side.

questions.stem: A sphere has a surface area of 36π. Its volume is
questions.explain: Surface area is 4πr², so 4πr² = 36π, r² = 9 and r = 3. Volume = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π(27) = 36π. 108π leaves out the 1/3, 288π uses πr² = 36π to get r = 6, 27π is just πr³, and 12π uses r² instead of r³.

questions.stem: If every edge of a cube is increased by 50%, its volume increases by
questions.explain: The new edge is 1.5 times the old, so the new volume is 1.5³ = 3.375 times the old. That is an increase of 3.375 − 1 = 2.375, or 237.5%. 150% multiplies 50% by 3, 125% is the increase in surface area (1.5² − 1), 337.5% gives the new volume as a percent of the old rather than the increase, and 50% assumes volume changes like length.

questions.stem: In right triangle ABC with right angle C, sin A = 5/13. tan A is
questions.explain: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse, so the opposite side is 5 and the hypotenuse 13. The adjacent side is √(169 − 25) = 12. tan A = opposite/adjacent = 5/12. 12/5 is cot A (upside down), 12/13 is cos A, 13/5 is csc A, and 13/12 is sec A.

questions.stem: If θ is an acute angle and tan θ = 3/4, then sin θ + cos θ =
questions.explain: tan θ = 3/4 means opposite 3 and adjacent 4, so the hypotenuse is 5. Then sin θ = 3/5 and cos θ = 4/5, and their sum is 7/5. 7/4 divides by the adjacent side, 1 assumes sin θ + cos θ = 1 (it is sin²θ + cos²θ that equals 1), 12/25 is the product, and 5/7 is the reciprocal.

questions.stem: log₂ 32 − log₃ (1/9) is equal to
questions.explain: log₂ 32 = 5 because 2⁵ = 32, and log₃ (1/9) = −2 because 3⁻² = 1/9. So 5 − (−2) = 7. 3 treats log₃ (1/9) as +2, −7 slips the sign of the whole answer, and 9/2 and 11/2 confuse 1/9 with 9^(−1/2), treating log₃ (1/9) as 1/2 or −1/2.

questions.stem: If logₓ 64 = 3/2, then x =
questions.explain: Rewrite in exponential form: x^(3/2) = 64. Raise both sides to the 2/3 power: x = 64^(2/3) = (∛64)² = 4² = 16. Check: 16^(3/2) = (√16)³ = 64. 96 multiplies 64 by 3/2, 4 stops at the cube root, 512 calculates 64^(3/2), and 8 takes the square root.

questions.stem: If log 2 = a and log 3 = b, then log 72 =
questions.explain: 72 = 8 × 9 = 2³ × 3². The log of a product is the sum of the logs, and the log of a power brings the exponent down: log 72 = 3 log 2 + 2 log 3 = 3a + 2b. 2a + 3b swaps the exponents (that is log 108), 6ab multiplies instead of adding, a³ + b² cubes and squares the logs instead of multiplying them, and 3a + 3b is log 216.

questions.stem: How many prime numbers are between 50 and 80?
questions.explain: The primes are 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73 and 79, so there are 7. The usual traps are 51 (3 × 17), 57 (3 × 19), 69 (3 × 23) and 77 (7 × 11): counting any of these gives 8 or 9, and missing one of the real primes gives 6 or 5.

questions.stem: The least common multiple of 18, 24 and 30 is
questions.explain: Factor each number: 18 = 2 × 3², 24 = 2³ × 3 and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2³ × 3² × 5 = 360. 720 is a common multiple but not the least, 180 uses 2² instead of 2³, 6 is the greatest common factor, and 12,960 is the product of the three numbers.

questions.stem: Which number is divisible by both 6 and 9 but not by 4?
questions.explain: 126 is even and its digits add to 9, so it is divisible by 2, 3 and 9, and therefore by 6 and 9; its last two digits, 26, are not divisible by 4, so 126 is not. 108 and 144 are divisible by 4, 84 fails the test for 9 (digit sum 12), and 135 is odd, so it is not divisible by 6.

questions.stem: If m is an odd integer and n is an even integer, which expression must be odd?
questions.explain: An odd number squared is odd (m²), and odd + even is odd, so m² + n is always odd. mn is even because one factor is even, m + 3 is odd + odd = even, n² + 2m is even + even = even, and (m + n)(m − 1) has the even factor m − 1, so it is even.

questions.stem: Which of the following is irrational?
questions.explain: √27 = 3√3, so (√27)/3 = √3, which cannot be written as a ratio of integers. √0.81 = 0.9, a repeating decimal such as 0.1212... equals a fraction (12/99), √(50/2) = √25 = 5, and ∛(−8/27) = −2/3, so all of those are rational.

questions.stem: For the data 7, 3, 9, 3, 12, 5, 8, 3, 10, 6, the median minus the mode is
questions.explain: Sort the data: 3, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. With ten values, the median is the average of the 5th and 6th values, (6 + 7)/2 = 6.5. The mode (most frequent value) is 3, so 6.5 − 3 = 3.5. 3.6 uses the mean (66/10 = 6.6) instead of the median, 5.5 takes the middle of the unsorted list (12 and 5), 9 is the range, and 0.1 is mean minus median.

questions.stem: If n is an odd integer, which of the following must be divisible by 8?
questions.explain: n² − 1 = (n − 1)(n + 1) is the product of two consecutive even numbers, one of which is a multiple of 4, so it is always a multiple of 8 (n = 3, 5, 7 give 8, 24, 48). 2n + 6 and 3n + 5 both give 8 for n = 1 but fail at n = 3 (12 and 14), the mistake of testing a single value. n² + 3 is always a multiple of 4 but never of 8 (4, 12, 28), and 4n is only a multiple of 4 because n is odd.

Write both sides as powers of 2: 4^(x + 1) = 2^(2x + 2) and 8^(x − 1) = 2^(3x − 3). Set the exponents equal: 2x + 2 = 3x − 3, so x = 5. 3 multiplies the bases by the exponents (4(x + 1) = 8(x − 1)), 4 writes 4^(x + 1) as 2^(2x + 1), −1 distributes the 3 as 3x + 3, and −5 slips the sign when solving.

questions.stem: 2¹⁰ + 2¹⁰ + 2¹⁰ + 2¹⁰ is equal to
questions.explain: Four equal terms are 4 × 2¹⁰, and 4 = 2², so the sum is 2² × 2¹⁰ = 2¹². 2⁴⁰ multiplies the exponents by 4, 8¹⁰ adds the bases, 2¹¹ treats four copies as two (2 × 2¹⁰), and 8⁴⁰ adds both the bases and the exponents.

questions.stem: For any integer n, (3ⁿ⁺² − 3ⁿ) ÷ 3ⁿ is equal to
questions.explain: Factor 3ⁿ out of the numerator: 3ⁿ(3² − 1) = 3ⁿ × 8, and dividing by 3ⁿ leaves 8. 9 drops the − 3ⁿ term, 2 subtracts the exponents (n + 2 − n) and stops, 6 computes 3² − 3, and 10 factors with the wrong sign, 3ⁿ(3² + 1).

questions.stem: (√5 + √3)² is equal to
questions.explain: Use (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²: 5 + 2√15 + 3 = 8 + 2√15. 8 squares each term and forgets the middle term, 8 + √15 forgets the 2 in 2ab, 64 squares 5 + 3 instead of √5 + √3, and 8 + 2√8 adds the radicands instead of multiplying them.

Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate √6 + √2. The denominator becomes 6 − 2 = 4. The numerator is (√6 + √2)² = 6 + 2√12 + 2 = 8 + 4√3. Then (8 + 4√3)/4 = 2 + √3. 2 drops the middle term, 1 + √3/2 adds 6 + 2 in the denominator instead of subtracting, 4 + 2√3 takes the denominator as 6 − 4 = 2, and 2 − √3 squares √6 − √2 in the numerator instead of √6 + √2.

questions.stem: The solution set of √(2x + 7) = x + 2 is
questions.explain: Square both sides: 2x + 7 = x² + 4x + 4, so x² + 2x − 3 = 0 and (x + 3)(x − 1) = 0, giving x = −3 or x = 1. Check both: x = 1 gives √9 = 3 = 1 + 2, which works; x = −3 gives √1 = 1 but −3 + 2 = −1, so it is extraneous. Keeping both skips the check, −3 only keeps the wrong root, and 3 only and −1 only come from factoring x² + 2x − 3 as (x − 3)(x + 1).

questions.stem: The solution of x² − x − 12 < 0 is
questions.explain: Factor: (x − 4)(x + 3) < 0. The product is negative only between the roots −3 and 4, so −3 < x < 4. Check x = 0: −12 < 0. x < −3 or x > 4 is where the product is positive, −4 < x < 3 reverses the signs of the roots, x < 4 ignores the lower root, and −3 ≤ x ≤ 4 includes the endpoints, where the expression equals 0, not less than 0.

questions.stem: How many integers x satisfy 3 < 2x − 5 ≤ 11?
questions.explain: Add 5 to every part: 8 < 2x ≤ 16. Divide by 2: 4 < x ≤ 8. The integers are 5, 6, 7 and 8, so there are 4. 5 includes 4 by treating < as ≤, 3 excludes 8 by treating ≤ as <, 8 counts the integers from 8 to 16 without dividing by 2 (9 through 16), and 6 counts the integers from 3 to 8.

questions.stem: If −2 ≤ a ≤ 3 and −1 ≤ b ≤ 4, what is the greatest possible value of a − b?
questions.explain: To make a − b as large as possible, take the largest a and the smallest b: 3 − (−1) = 4. −1 uses the largest b (3 − 4), 7 adds the largest values (3 + 4), 6 subtracts the smallest a from the largest b (4 − (−2)), and 1 subtracts the upper limits of b and a the other way round (4 − 3).

Expand: 3x − 6 − 2x + 10 = 4x + 4 − 9, so x + 4 = 4x − 5. Then 9 = 3x and x = 3. Check: 3(1) − 2(−2) = 7 and 4(4) − 9 = 7. −3 slips a sign when moving terms (9 = −3x), 4 writes 4(x + 1) as 4x + 1, 0 drops the −9, and −11/3 distributes −2(x − 5) as −2x − 10.

questions.stem: If x + y = 10, y + z = 14 and x + z = 12, then x + y + z =
questions.explain: Adding all three equations counts each variable twice: 2x + 2y + 2z = 36, so x + y + z = 18. Check: x = 4, y = 6, z = 8. 36 forgets to divide by 2, 12 is the middle equation's total, 24 adds only two equations, and 14 takes the largest total.

questions.stem: For what value of k does the system 2x + ky = 5 and 4x + 6y = 7 have no solution?
questions.explain: Two lines have no common point when they are parallel but distinct. The second equation's x-coefficient is twice the first's, so the y-coefficients must also be in a 2:1 ratio: 6 = 2k, giving k = 3. Then the constants 5 and 7 are not in a 2:1 ratio, so the lines are distinct. 6 copies the coefficient, −3 slips a sign, 12 doubles instead of halving, and 3/2 divides by 4.

questions.stem: The vertex of the parabola y = 2x² − 12x + 7 is
questions.explain: The vertex is at x = −b/(2a) = 12/4 = 3, and y = 2(9) − 12(3) + 7 = 18 − 36 + 7 = −11. (−3, 61) takes x = b/(2a), (3, 7) uses the y-intercept as the y-value, (6, 7) uses x = −b/a, and (−3, −11) keeps the right y-value but flips the sign of x.

questions.stem: One root of x² + kx − 24 = 0 is 4. What is the value of k?
questions.explain: Substitute x = 4: 16 + 4k − 24 = 0, so 4k = 8 and k = 2. Check with the other root: the product of the roots is −24, so it is −6, and the sum 4 + (−6) = −2 equals −k. −2 gives the sum of the roots, not k, −10 uses +24 in place of −24, 10 makes that error and also flips the sign, and 6 is the size of the other root.

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² − 3x, then f(a + 1) − f(a) =
questions.explain: f(a + 1) = (a + 1)² − 3(a + 1) = a² + 2a + 1 − 3a − 3 = a² − a − 2. Subtract f(a) = a² − 3a: (a² − a − 2) − (a² − 3a) = 2a − 2. 2a + 1 drops the −3x terms, 1 treats f(a + 1) as f(a) + 1, −2 writes (a + 1)² as a² + 1, and 2a forgets the constant terms.

questions.stem: The domain of f(x) = √(6 − 2x) ÷ (x − 1) is
questions.explain: The square root needs 6 − 2x ≥ 0, so x ≤ 3, and the denominator needs x ≠ 1. x ≤ 3 forgets the denominator, x ≥ 3 forgets to flip the inequality when dividing by −2, x < 3 wrongly excludes 3 (√0 = 0 is allowed), and x ≠ 1 ignores the square root.

questions.stem: What is the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (7, 2) and (4, 8)?
questions.explain: The base from (1, 2) to (7, 2) is horizontal with length 6. The height is the vertical distance from y = 2 to y = 8, which is 6. Area = (1/2)(6)(6) = 18. 36 forgets the 1/2, 9 halves twice, 24 uses a height of 8 (the y-coordinate), and 12 uses a base of 4 (the x-coordinate of the top vertex).

questions.stem: The line 5x − 2y = 20 crosses the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B. If O is the origin, what is the area of triangle OAB?
questions.explain: At A, y = 0, so x = 4. At B, x = 0, so −2y = 20 and y = −10. The legs of the right triangle are 4 and 10, so the area is (1/2)(4)(10) = 20. 40 forgets the 1/2, 10 uses the y-intercept as the area, 14 adds the legs, and 50 uses an x-intercept of 10 (20 ÷ 2).

questions.stem: The circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0 has
questions.explain: Complete the squares: (x² − 6x + 9) + (y² + 4y + 4) = 12 + 9 + 4, so (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25. The center is (3, −2) and the radius is √25 = 5. (−3, 2) flips the signs, radius 25 forgets the square root, √12 forgets to add the 9 and 4, and (6, −4) uses the coefficients without halving them.

questions.stem: The line through (2, k) and (k, 8) has a slope of 2. What is k?
questions.explain: Slope = (8 − k)/(k − 2) = 2, so 8 − k = 2k − 4, 12 = 3k and k = 4. Check: (2, 4) to (4, 8) rises 4 over a run of 2. 6 puts run over rise ((k − 2)/(8 − k) = 2), 2 makes the denominator 0, 10/3 multiplies only the k by 2 (8 − k = 2k − 2), and 8/3 drops the −2 from the denominator.

questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is one-fifth of each interior angle. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explain: Interior + exterior = 180°, and interior = 5 × exterior, so 6 × exterior = 180° and the exterior angle is 30°. Exterior angles sum to 360°, so there are 360/30 = 12 sides. 10 uses 36° (one-fifth of 180), 6 counts the parts of the 180°, 5 uses the ratio itself, and 30 is the exterior angle, not the number of sides.

questions.stem: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is 30° more than each base angle. What is the largest angle of the triangle?
questions.explain: Let each base angle be b. Then b + b + (b + 30) = 180, so 3b = 150 and b = 50°. The vertex angle is 80°, the largest. 50° is a base angle, 70° reverses the relationship (base angles 30° more than the vertex), 100° is the supplement of the vertex angle, and 105° counts only one base angle (b + b + 30 = 180 gives b = 75).

questions.stem: A 25-foot ladder leans against a wall with its foot 7 feet from the wall. The foot slips 8 feet farther from the wall. How far does the top of the ladder slide down the wall?
questions.explain: At first the top is √(25² − 7²) = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 feet up. After slipping, the foot is 15 feet out and the top is √(625 − 225) = √400 = 20 feet up. It slid 24 − 20 = 4 feet. 8 feet assumes the top moves as far as the foot, 20 feet and 24 feet are the heights after and before rather than the change, and 7 feet repeats the starting distance.

questions.stem: A square has a diagonal of length 10. What is its area?
questions.explain: The diagonal of a square with side s is s√2, so s = 10/√2 = 5√2 and the area is (5√2)² = 50. Shortcut: area = d²/2 = 100/2 = 50. 100 squares the diagonal, 25 halves twice, 50√2 forgets to square the √2, and 10√2 multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.stem: A figure is a 10-by-6 rectangle with a semicircle attached outward along one of its 6-unit sides. What is the figure's total area?
questions.explain: The rectangle is 10 × 6 = 60. The semicircle's diameter is 6, so its radius is 3, and its area is (1/2)π(3²) = 4.5π.
